lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: آه، أَنتَ مَن أَرسَلَتهُ أَميرَة! السَّلامُ عَلَيْكُم
lines.english: Ah, you're the one Amira sent! Peace be upon you.
lines.transliteration: aah, anta man arsalathu amiira! as-salaamu alaykum

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا الشَّيْخ يوسُف، عالِمُ القَرية. أُعَلِّمُ اللُّغَة العَرَبِيَّة
lines.english: I am Scholar Yusuf, the village scholar. I teach the Arabic language.
lines.transliteration: ana ash-shaykh yuusuf, aalimu al-qarya. u'allimu al-lugha al-arabiyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَميرَة أَخبَرَتني أَنَّكَ تَعَلَّمتَ 'مَرْحَبا' — مُمتاز! لِنَتَعَلَّم المَزيد
lines.english: Amira told me you learned 'marhaba' — excellent! Let's learn more.
lines.transliteration: amiira akhbaratnii annaka ta'allamta 'marhaba' — mumtaaz! linata'allam al-maziid

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مُمْتاز! لِنَبْدَأ بِالتَّحِيّات — أَهَمّ الكَلِمات
lines.english: Excellent! Let's start with greetings — the most important words.
lines.transliteration: mumtaaz! linabda' bit-tahiyyaat — ahamm al-kalimaat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الكَلِمَة الأولى: سَلام — تَحِيَّة المُسلِمين
lines.english: The first word: Salaam — the Muslim greeting (peace).
lines.transliteration: al-kalima al-uulaa: salaam — tahiyyat al-muslimiin

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الكَلِمَة الثّانِيَة: شُكْراً — نَقولُها لِلشُّكر
lines.english: The second word: Shukran — we say it to give thanks.
lines.transliteration: al-kalima ath-thaaniya: shukran — naquuluhaa lish-shukr

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الآن دَعْنا نَخْتَبِر ما تَعَلَّمْت!
lines.english: Now let's test what you've learned!
lines.transliteration: al-aan da'naa nakhtabir maa ta'allamta!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحسَنت! أَنتَ مُتَعَلِّمٌ سَريع. عُد إلَيَّ لِتَتَعَلَّم المَزيد مِنَ التَّحِيّات
lines.english: Well done! You're a fast learner. Come back to me to learn more greetings.
lines.transliteration: ahsant! anta muta'allimun sarii'. ud ilayya litata'allam al-maziid min at-tahiyyaat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَتَكَلَّم مَع فاطِمَة التّاجِرَة وَخالِد الطّالِب أَيضاً — كُلُّهُم يُعَلِّمونَك!
lines.english: And talk to Merchant Fatima and Student Khalid too — they all teach you!
lines.transliteration: wa takallam ma'a faatima at-taajira wa khaalid at-taalib aydan — kulluhum yu'allimuunak!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلاً بِكَ مَرَّة أُخرى! لِنَتَعَلَّم المَزيد
lines.english: Welcome back! Let's learn more.
lines.transliteration: ahlan bika marra ukhraa! linata'allam al-maziid

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلاً — كَلِمَة لِلتَرحيب
lines.english: Ahlan — a word of welcome.
lines.transliteration: ahlan — kalima lit-tarhiib

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عَفْوًا — تَعني 'لا شُكْر عَلى واجِب'
lines.english: Afwan — it means 'you're welcome'.
lines.transliteration: afwan — ta'nii 'laa shukr alaa waajib'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَعَ السَّلامَة — عِندَ الوَداع
lines.english: Ma'a salama — when saying goodbye.
lines.transliteration: ma'a as-salaama — inda al-wadaa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: صَباحُ الخَير — في الصَّباح
lines.english: Sabah al-khayr — in the morning.
lines.transliteration: sabaah al-khayr — fis-sabaah

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عَظيم! أَنتَ تَتَعَلَّم بِسُرعَة
lines.english: Great! You're learning quickly.
lines.transliteration: aziim! anta tata'allam bisur'a

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَساءُ الخَير — في المَساء
lines.english: Masa' al-khayr — in the evening.
lines.transliteration: masaa' al-khayr — fil-masaa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: نَعَم — يَعني 'أَيوه'
lines.english: Na'am — means 'yes'.
lines.transliteration: na'am — ya'nii 'aywa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لا — عَكْسُها
lines.english: La — its opposite.
lines.transliteration: laa — aksuha

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذِهِ واحَة الحُروف — مَكانٌ لِتَعَلُّم العَرَبِيَّة
lines.english: This is the Oasis of Letters — a place for learning Arabic.
lines.transliteration: haadhihi waahat al-huruuf — makaanun li-ta'allum al-arabiyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَكَلَّم مَع النّاس هُنا وَسَتَتَعَلَّم كَلِمات جَديدَة
lines.english: Talk to the people here and you will learn new words.
lines.transliteration: takallam ma'a an-naas hunaa wa satata'allam kalimaat jadiida

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: فاطِمَة التّاجِرَة عِنْدَها كَلِمات السُّوق
lines.english: Fatima the merchant has market words.
lines.transliteration: faatima at-taajira indahaa kalimaat as-suuq

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَخالِد الطّالِب يُحِبّ المُسابَقات
lines.english: And Khalid the student likes quizzes.
lines.transliteration: wa khaalid at-taalib yuhibb al-musaabaqaat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل أَنتَ مُسْتَعِدّ لِتَعَلُّم الحُروف؟
lines.english: Are you ready to learn the letters?
lines.transliteration: hal anta musta'idd li-ta'allum al-huruuf?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: السَّلامُ عَلَيْكُم، طالِبَ العِلْم. بِسْمِ اللَّه
lines.english: Peace be upon you, seeker of knowledge. In the name of God.
lines.transliteration: as-salaamu alaykum, taalib al-ilm. bismillaah

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عَمَّ تُريدُ أَن تَتَكَلَّم؟
lines.english: What would you like to discuss?
lines.transliteration: amma turiidu an tatakallam?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل تَعْلَمُ أَنَّنا نُقَدِّمُ دُروسًا في قَواعِدِ اللُّغَةِ العَرَبِيَّة؟
lines.english: Did you know we offer lessons in Arabic grammar rules?
lines.transliteration: hal taʿlam annanā nuqaddim durūsan fī qawāʿid al-lugha al-ʿarabiyya?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: القَواعِدُ تُساعِدُكَ على فَهْمِ بِنْيَةِ الجُمَلِ وَالكَلِمات
lines.english: Grammar helps you understand sentence and word structure.
lines.transliteration: al-qawāʿid tusāʿiduka ʿalā fahm binyat al-jumal wa-l-kalimāt

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: جَرِّبْها! اِفْتَحْ قائِمَةَ الإيقافِ المُؤَقَّتِ واخْتَرْ 'أَنْشِطَة'
lines.english: Try it! Open the pause menu and choose 'Activities'.
lines.transliteration: jarribhā! iftaḥ qāʾimat al-īqāf al-muʾaqqat wa-khtar 'anshiṭa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: التَّحِيّاتُ أَساسُ الأَدَب. بِسْمِ اللَّه، لِنَبْدَأ
lines.english: Greetings are the foundation of manners. In God's name, let us begin.
lines.transliteration: at-tahiyyaatu asaas al-adab. bismillaah, linabda'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: واحَةُ الحُروفِ مَكانٌ قَديمٌ جِدّاً
lines.english: The Oasis of Letters is a very ancient place.
lines.transliteration: waahat al-huruuf makaanun qadiimun jiddan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هُنا تَعَلَّمَ العُلَماءُ الأَوائِلُ اللُّغَةَ العَرَبِيَّة
lines.english: Here the first scholars learned the Arabic language.
lines.transliteration: hunaa ta'allama al-ulamaa' al-awaa'il al-lugha al-arabiyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لَدَيَّ مَهَمَّة لَكَ يا طالِب
lines.english: I have a task for you, student.
lines.transliteration: ladayya mahamma laka ya taalib

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِذْهَب وَتَعَلَّم عَشْرَ كَلِمات جَديدَة
lines.english: Go and learn ten new words.
lines.transliteration: idh-hab wa ta'allam ashr kalimaat jadiida

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: في الخَطِّ العَرَبيِّ سِتَّةُ أُصولٍ كَبيرَة
lines.english: In Arabic calligraphy there are six great canonical scripts
lines.transliteration: fil-khatt al-arabi sittat usul kabira

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: النَّسخ وَالثُّلُث وَالرِّقعَة وَالدِّيواني وَالفارِسي وَالكوفي
lines.english: Naskh, Thuluth, Ruq'ah, Diwani, Farsi, and Kufi
lines.transliteration: an-naskh wath-thuluth war-ruq'a wad-diwani wal-farisi wal-kufi

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ابنُ مُقلَة في القَرنِ العاشِر وَضَعَ قَواعِدَ النِّسَب
lines.english: Ibn Muqla in the 10th century established the proportional rules
lines.transliteration: ibn muqla fil-qarn al-'ashir wada'a qawa'id an-nisab
lines.culturalNote: Ibn Muqla (886-940 CE) created the proportional system that standardized Arabic calligraphy. Each letter is measured in dots relative to the alif.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كُلُّ حَرفٍ يُقاسُ بِنِقاطٍ نِسبَةً إلى الأَلِف
lines.english: Every letter is measured in dots relative to the alif
lines.transliteration: kullu harf yuqas bi-niqat nisbatan ila al-alif

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الشِّعرُ عِندَ المُتَنَبّي بَلَغَ ذُروَتَهُ — 'أَنا الَّذي نَظَرَ الأَعمى إلى أَدَبي'
lines.english: Poetry reached its peak with Al-Mutanabbi — 'I am he whose literature the blind can see'
lines.transliteration: ash-shi'r 'inda al-mutanabbi balagha dhurwatahu
lines.culturalNote: Al-Mutanabbi (915-965 CE) is considered the greatest Arabic poet. His name means 'the one who claimed to be a prophet' — a childhood nickname that stuck.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بِسمِ اللَّه! اليَومَ سَنَتَعَلَّمُ قاعِدَةً عَظيمَة في العَرَبِيَّة
lines.english: In God's name! Today we will learn a great rule in Arabic.
lines.transliteration: bismillaah! al-yawma sanata'allamu qaa'idatan aziima fil-arabiyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لَيسَ في العَرَبِيَّةِ فِعلٌ لِـ'كانَ' في المُضارِع — أَنا طالِبٌ، لَيسَ 'أَنا أَكونُ طالِباً'
lines.english: Arabic has no verb 'to be' in the present tense — 'ana taalib' means 'I am a student', not 'I am being a student'.
lines.transliteration: laysa fil-arabiyya fi'lun li-kaana fil-mudaari' — ana taalib, laysa 'ana akuunu taaliban'
lines.culturalNote: Arabic omits the copula (verb 'to be') in present tense nominal sentences. This is called a 'jumlah ismiyya' — a noun sentence. English learners often struggle with this elegant simplicity.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قُل مَعي: أَنا طالِبٌ — هَذِهِ جُملَةٌ اسمِيَّة
lines.english: Say with me: Ana taalib — this is a nominal sentence.
lines.transliteration: qul ma'ii: ana taalib — haadhihi jumlatun ismiyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الآن أَنتَ: مَن أَنتَ؟ قُل اسمَك بِالعَرَبِيَّة
lines.english: Now you: who are you? Say your name in Arabic.
lines.transliteration: al-aan anta: man anta? qul ismaka bil-arabiyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحسَنت! في العَرَبِيَّةِ الكَلِماتُ لَها مُذَكَّر وَمُؤَنَّث
lines.english: Well done! In Arabic, words have masculine and feminine forms.
lines.transliteration: ahsant! fil-arabiyya al-kalimaat lahaa mudhakkar wa mu'annath

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كِتابٌ — مُذَكَّر. مَكتَبَةٌ — مُؤَنَّث. تَلاحَظُ حَرفَ التّاء في النِّهايَة؟
lines.english: Kitab — masculine. Maktaba — feminine. Notice the 'ta' letter at the end?
lines.transliteration: kitaabun — mudhakkar. maktabatun — mu'annath. talaahazu harf at-taa' fin-nihaaya?
lines.culturalNote: The taa marbuuta (ة) marks feminine nouns in Arabic. It was invented by early Arab grammarians to standardize gender marking, making Arabic one of the most systematic languages for gender in grammar.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كِتاب — كِتابان — كُتُب. هَذا الجَمع! الجَمعُ التَّكسيريّ
lines.english: Kitab — two books — books. This is the plural! The broken plural.
lines.transliteration: kitaab — kitaabayn — kutub. haadhaa al-jam'! al-jam' at-taksiiriyy

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الجَمعُ التَّكسيريُّ يُغَيِّرُ شَكلَ الكَلِمَة مِن الداخِل — هَذا فَريدٌ في العَرَبِيَّة
lines.english: The broken plural changes the shape of the word from within — this is unique to Arabic.
lines.transliteration: al-jam' at-taksiiriyyu yughayyiru shakl al-kalima min ad-daakhil — haadhaa fariidun fil-arabiyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لا تَقلَق! حَتّى العُلَماءُ الكِبارُ بَدَأوا مِن الصِّفر
lines.english: Do not worry! Even the great scholars started from zero.
lines.transliteration: laa taqlaq! hatta al-ulama al-kibaar bada'uu min as-sifr

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الإمامُ سيبَوَيه كانَ فارِسِيَّ الأَصل وَأَصبَحَ أَعظَمَ نَحويٍّ عَرَبيّ
lines.english: Imam Sibawayhi was of Persian origin and became the greatest Arab grammarian.
lines.transliteration: al-imaam sibawayhi kaana farisiyya al-asl wa asbaha a'dhama nahwiyyin arabii
lines.culturalNote: Sibawayhi (c.760-796 CE) wrote 'Al-Kitab' — the foundational work of Arabic grammar. He was Persian, proving that mastery of Arabic belongs to all who pursue it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العِلمُ يَحتاجُ صَبراً. بِسمِ اللَّه، لِنُكمِل
lines.english: Knowledge requires patience. In God's name, let us continue.
lines.transliteration: al-ilm yahtaaju sabran. bismillaah, linukmil

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بِسمِ اللَّه! هَل تَعلَمُ مِن أَينَ جاءَت كَلِمَةُ 'algorithm'؟
lines.english: In God's name! Do you know where the word 'algorithm' came from?
lines.transliteration: bismillaah! hal ta'lamu min ayna jaa'at kalimat 'algorithm'?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مِن اسمِ العالِمِ مُحَمَّد بنِ موسى الخَوارِزميّ
lines.english: From the name of the scholar Muhammad ibn Musa al-Khwarizmi.
lines.transliteration: min ism al-aalim muhammad ibn muusa al-khwaarizmi
lines.culturalNote: Al-Khwarizmi (780-850 CE) was the father of algebra. His book 'Al-Kitab al-Mukhtasar fi Hisab al-Jabr' gave us the word 'algebra' (al-jabr). His name, Latinized as 'Algoritmi', became 'algorithm'.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَكَلِمَةُ 'algebra' مِن 'الجَبر' — عُنوانُ كِتابِهِ العَظيم
lines.english: And 'algebra' from 'al-jabr' — the title of his great book.
lines.transliteration: wa kalimat 'algebra' min 'al-jabr' — unwaanu kitaabihi al-aziim
lines.culturalNote: The word 'algebra' comes from 'al-jabr wa al-muqabala' (reunion of broken parts and balancing). Al-Khwarizmi also introduced the Indian zero concept to the Islamic world.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العُلَماءُ العَرَبُ نَقَلوا العِلمَ وَأَضافوا إِلَيه. هَذا شَرَفُنا
lines.english: Arab scholars transmitted knowledge and added to it. This is our honor.
lines.transliteration: al-ulama al-arab naqalu al-ilm wa adaafuu ilayh. haadhaa sharafunaa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَلَّم العَرَبِيَّة وَسَتَفتَحُ لَكَ أَبوابَ الحِكمَة القَديمَة
lines.english: Learn Arabic and it will open for you the doors of ancient wisdom.
lines.transliteration: ta'allam al-arabiyya wa sataftahu laka abwaab al-hikma al-qadiima

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَرْحَباً! أَنا فاطِمَة، صاحِبَة هَذا الدُّكّان
lines.english: Hello! I am Fatima, owner of this shop.
lines.transliteration: marhaban! ana faatima, saahibat haadha ad-dukkaan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عِنْدي أَشْياء كَثيرَة. هَل تُريدُ أَن تَتَعَلَّم أَسْماءَها؟
lines.english: I have many things. Do you want to learn their names?
lines.transliteration: indii ashyaa' kathiira. hal turiidu an tata'allama asmaa'ahaa?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: طَيِّب! هَذا يُسَمّى دُكّان
lines.english: Good! This is called a shop.
lines.transliteration: tayyib! haadha yusammaa dukkaan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَالمَكان الكَبير يُسَمّى سُوق
lines.english: And the big place is called a market.
lines.transliteration: wal-makaan al-kabiir yusammaa suuq

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَهَذا فُلوس — نَقود
lines.english: And this is money — currency.
lines.transliteration: wa haadha fuluus — nuquud

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الآن اِخْتَبِر نَفسَك!
lines.english: Now test yourself!
lines.transliteration: al-aan ikhtabir nafsak!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلاً مَرَّة أُخرى! لِنُكْمِل دَرسَنا
lines.english: Hello again! Let's continue our lesson.
lines.transliteration: ahlan marra ukhraa! linukmil darsanaa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ثَمَن — يَعني السِّعْر
lines.english: Thaman — means the price.
lines.transliteration: thaman — ya'nii as-si'r

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: رَخيص — يَعني السِّعْر قَليل
lines.english: Rakhiis — means the price is low.
lines.transliteration: rakhiis — ya'nii as-si'r qaliil

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: غالي — يَعني السِّعْر كَبير
lines.english: Ghaali — means the price is high.
lines.transliteration: ghaali — ya'nii as-si'r kabiir

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِشْتَرى — يَعني يَأخُذ بِفُلوس
lines.english: Ishtara — means to take with money (to buy).
lines.transliteration: ishtaraa — ya'nii ya'khudh bi-fuluus

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ما شاء الله! تاجِر مُمتاز!
lines.english: Mashallah! An excellent merchant!
lines.transliteration: maa shaa'allaah! taajir mumtaaz!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: باعَ — عَكْس اِشتَرى
lines.english: Baa'a — the opposite of bought (to sell).
lines.transliteration: baa'a — aks ishtaraa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ذَهَب — المَعدِن الأَصفَر الثَّمين
lines.english: Dhahab — the precious yellow metal (gold).
lines.transliteration: dhahab — al-ma'din al-asfar ath-thamiin

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: فِضَّة — المَعدِن الأَبيَض
lines.english: Fidda — the white metal (silver).
lines.transliteration: fidda — al-ma'din al-abyad

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلاً يا زَبون! يَلّا، ماذا تُريد اليَوم؟
lines.english: Welcome, customer! Come on, what do you want today?
lines.transliteration: ahlan ya zabuun! yalla, maadha turiid al-yawm?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل تُريدُ طَريقَةً مُمْتِعَةً لِلتَّدَرُّب على المُفْرَدات؟
lines.english: Want a fun way to practice vocabulary?
lines.transliteration: hal turīd ṭarīqa mumtiʿa li-t-tadarrub ʿalā al-mufradāt?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لَدَيْنا أَلْعابٌ صَغيرَةٌ — لُعْبَة البَحْثِ عَن الكَلِمات وَأَكْثَر!
lines.english: We have mini-games — word search and more!
lines.transliteration: ladaynā alʿāb ṣaghīra — luʿbat al-baḥth ʿan al-kalimāt wa-akthar!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِفْتَحْ قائِمَةَ الإيقاف وَاخْتَرْ 'أَنْشِطَة' ثُمَّ 'أَلْعاب'
lines.english: Open the pause menu and choose 'Activities' then 'Mini-Games'.
lines.transliteration: iftaḥ qāʾimat al-īqāf wa-khtar 'anshiṭa' thumma 'alʿāb'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يَلّا! سَأُعَلِّمُكَ كَلِمات السُّوق
lines.english: Come on! I'll teach you market words.
lines.transliteration: yalla! sa-u'allimuka kalimaat as-suuq

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سَمِعْتُ أَنَّ التّاجِرَ حَسَن عِندَهُ بَضائِع جَديدَة
lines.english: I heard that trader Hassan has new goods.
lines.transliteration: sami'tu anna at-taajir hasan indahu badaa'i' jadiida

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَالسُّوقُ مَشْغول جِدّاً هَذِهِ الأَيّام!
lines.english: And the market is very busy these days!
lines.transliteration: was-suuq mashghuul jiddan haadhihi al-ayyaam!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحْتاجُ مُساعَدَة! هَل تَسْتَطيعُ إِيجادَ زَبائِن لي؟
lines.english: I need help! Can you find customers for me?
lines.transliteration: ahtaaju musaa'ada! hal tastatii'u ijaad zabaa'in lii?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل تَعلَم أَنَّ طَريقَ الحَريرِ كانَ يَمُرُّ مِن هُنا؟
lines.english: Did you know the Silk Road passed through here?
lines.transliteration: hal ta'lam anna tariq al-harir kana yamurru min huna?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: التُّجّارُ العَرَبُ نَقَلوا الأَرقامَ إلى أوروبا
lines.english: Arab traders carried numerals to Europe
lines.transliteration: at-tujjaar al-arab naqalu al-arqaam ila urubba

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كَلِمَةُ 'خَوارِزمي' أَصبَحَت 'algorithm' بالإنجليزيَّة
lines.english: The word 'Khwarizmi' became 'algorithm' in English
lines.transliteration: kalimat 'khwarizmi' asbahat 'algorithm' bil-injiliziyya
lines.culturalNote: Al-Khwarizmi (780-850 CE) wrote the foundational text on algebra. His name, Latinized as 'Algoritmi', gave us the word 'algorithm'.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَكَلِمَةُ 'تَعريفَة' أَعطَت الإنجليزيَّة 'tariff'
lines.english: And 'ta'rifa' gave English the word 'tariff'
lines.transliteration: wa kalimat 'ta'rifa' a'tat al-injiliziyya 'tariff'
lines.culturalNote: Many English trade words come from Arabic: tariff (ta'rifa), magazine (makhazin), cotton (qutn), sugar (sukkar).

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يَلّا يا زَبون! أُعَلِّمُكَ فَنَّ المُساوَمَة. هَذا أَهَمُّ شَيء في السُّوق!
lines.english: Come on, customer! I'll teach you the art of bargaining. This is the most important thing in the market!
lines.transliteration: yalla ya zabuun! u'allimuka fann al-musaawama. haadhaa ahammu shay' fis-suuq!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَوَّلاً: لا تُظهِر اهتِمامَك. قُل: 'غالي' — هَذه أَداةٌ ذَهَبِيَّة
lines.english: First: don't show your interest. Say: 'ghaali' (expensive) — this is a golden tool.
lines.transliteration: awwalan: laa tudhir ihtimaamak. qul: 'ghaali' — haadhihi adaatun dhahabiyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ثُمَّ: 'هَذا رَخيص في السُّوق الآخَر!' — المُقارَنَة سِلاحٌ قَوِيّ
lines.english: Then: 'this is cheap at the other market!' — comparison is a powerful weapon.
lines.transliteration: thumma: 'haadhaa rakhiis fis-suuq al-aakhar!' — al-muqaarana silaahun qawii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَأَخيراً: اِمشِ! المَشيُ يَجعَلُ التّاجِرَ يُخَفِّضُ السِّعر — جَرِّب!
lines.english: And finally: walk away! Walking makes the trader lower the price — try it!
lines.transliteration: wa akhiiran: imshi! al-mashi yaj'al at-taajir yukhaffffid as-si'r — jarrib!

choices.english: How do I say 'lower the price'?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قُل: 'خَفِّض قَليلاً مِن فَضلَك!' — ثُمَّ اِبتَسِم
lines.english: Say: 'lower a little please!' — then smile.
lines.transliteration: qul: 'khaffid qaliilan min fadlak!' — thumma ibtasim

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: البَيعُ وَالشِّراءُ لُغَةٌ. التّاجِرُ الجَيِّدُ يُسمِع الآخَرين ما يُريدون أَن يَسمَعوه
lines.english: Buying and selling is a language. The good trader makes others hear what they want to hear.
lines.transliteration: al-bay' wash-shiraa' lugha. at-taajir al-jayyid yusmi' al-aakhariina maa yuriiduuna an yasma'uuh

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذِهِ حِكمَةُ سَبعِينَ سَنَة مِن التِّجارَة. يَلّا نَختَبِر!
lines.english: This is the wisdom of seventy years of trade. Come on, let's test!
lines.transliteration: haadhihi hikmat sab'iin sana min at-tijaara. yalla nakhtabir!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يَلّا يا زَبون! هَل تَعلَمُ كَم كَلِمَة أَنجليزيَّة جاءَت مِن لُغَتِنا؟
lines.english: Come on, customer! Do you know how many English words came from our language?
lines.transliteration: yalla ya zabuun! hal ta'lamu kam kalima injiliziyya jaa'at min lughatinaa?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: 'magazine' — مِن 'مَخازِن' يَعني مَكانُ التَّخزين. أَنا عَرِفتُ هَذا!
lines.english: 'Magazine' — from 'makhazin' meaning storehouse. I knew this one!
lines.transliteration: 'magazine' — min 'makhazin' ya'nii makaan at-takhziiin. ana arift haadhaa!
lines.culturalNote: The word 'magazine' comes from Arabic 'makhazin' (plural of makhzan — storehouse). Arab merchants stored goods in makhazin across the Silk Road trade routes.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: 'tariff' مِن 'تَعريفَة' — قائِمَةُ الأَسعار في السُّوق القَديم
lines.english: 'Tariff' from 'ta'rifa' — the price list in the old market.
lines.transliteration: 'tariff' min 'ta'rifa' — qaa'imat al-as'aar fis-suuq al-qadiim
lines.culturalNote: The word 'tariff' entered English through Spanish 'tarifa' from Arabic 'ta'rifa' (notification, schedule of prices). Arab merchants used ta'rifa notices posted at ports.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كَذَلِكَ 'mattress' مِن 'مَطرَح' وَ'sofa' مِن 'صُفَّة'!
lines.english: Also 'mattress' from 'matrah' and 'sofa' from 'suffa'!
lines.transliteration: kadhaalika 'mattress' min 'matrah' wa 'sofa' min 'suffa'!
lines.culturalNote: Many English household words are Arabic in origin: mattress (matrah — a place to throw), sofa (suffa — bench), jar (jarra), alcohol (al-kuhl), syrup (sharab).

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لُغَتُنا مَلِيئَةٌ بِالثَّروات — كَسُوقِنا! يَلّا!
lines.english: Our language is full of riches — like our market! Come on!
lines.transliteration: lughatunaa malii'atun bith-thawraat — kasuuqinaa! yalla!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَرْحَبا! أَنا خالِد. أَنا أَيْضاً أَتَعَلَّم
lines.english: Hello! I'm Khalid. I'm also learning.
lines.transliteration: marhaba! ana khaalid. ana aydan ata'allam

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل تُريدُ أَن نَتَدَرَّب مَعاً؟
lines.english: Do you want to practice together?
lines.transliteration: hal turiidu an nataddarab ma'an?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مُمْتاز! سَأَسْأَلُك عَشْر أَسْئِلَة
lines.english: Excellent! I'll ask you ten questions.
lines.transliteration: mumtaaz! sa-as'aluka ashr as'ila

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَرْحَبا! هَل أَنتَ جاهِز لِتَحَدّي اليَوم؟
lines.english: Hello! Are you ready for today's challenge?
lines.transliteration: marhaba! hal anta jaahiz li-tahaddii al-yawm?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يا هَلا! ماذا تُريد أَن نَفْعَل؟
lines.english: Hey there! What do you want to do?
lines.transliteration: ya halaa! maadha turiidu an naf'al?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يَلّا! خَلّينا نَتَدَرَّب!
lines.english: Let's go! Let's practice!
lines.transliteration: yalla! khalliina nataddarab!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا أَتَعَلَّمُ العَرَبِيَّةَ مِثْلَك!
lines.english: I'm learning Arabic just like you!
lines.transliteration: ana ata'allam al-arabiyya mithlak!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كُلَّ يَوم أَدْرُسُ مَعَ الشَّيْخ يوسُف
lines.english: Every day I study with Sheikh Yusuf.
lines.transliteration: kull yawm adrusu ma'a ash-shaykh yuusuf

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سَمِعْتُ أَنَّ هُناكَ كَنْز مَخْفيّ في الصَّحْراء!
lines.english: I heard there's a hidden treasure in the desert!
lines.transliteration: sami'tu anna hunaaka kanz makhfii fis-sahraa'!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لَكِنْ لا أَعْرِف إِذا كانَ هَذا صَحيح
lines.english: But I don't know if this is true.
lines.transliteration: laakin laa a'rif idhaa kaana haadhaa sahiih

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يا هَلا! أَنا غَلِطتُ اليَوم في الدَّرس — قُلتُ 'أَنا هُوَ ذاهِب' بَدَلاً مِن 'أَنا ذاهِب'!
lines.english: Hey there! I made a mistake in class today — I said 'I am he going' instead of 'I am going'!
lines.transliteration: ya halaa! ana ghalitt al-yawm fid-dars — qultu 'ana huwa dhaahib' badalan min 'ana dhaahib'!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الشَّيخُ يوسُف قالَ: لَيسَ في العَرَبِيَّةِ ضَميرٌ مُنفَصِلٌ مَعَ الفِعل في العادَة
lines.english: Sheikh Yusuf said: in Arabic, a separate pronoun doesn't usually go with the verb.
lines.transliteration: ash-shaykh yuusuf qaala: laysa fil-arabiyya damiir munfasil ma'a al-fi'l fil-'aada
lines.culturalNote: In Arabic, the subject pronoun is often embedded within the verb conjugation. 'Dhahaba' already means 'he went' — adding 'huwa' separately is redundant (though used for emphasis).

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذا صَعبٌ! أَنتَ بَالتَّأكيد تَغلَطُ أَيضاً أَحياناً، صَحّ؟
lines.english: This is hard! You definitely make mistakes sometimes too, right?
lines.transliteration: haadhaa sa'b! anta bittakiid taghlat aydan ahyaanan, sahh?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: المُهِمُّ أَنَّنا نُكمِل وَلا نَستَسلِم — هَذا ما يَقولُهُ الشَّيخ
lines.english: What matters is that we continue and don't give up — that's what the Sheikh says.
lines.transliteration: al-muhimm annana nukmil wa laa nastaslim — haadhaa maa yaquuluhu ash-shaykh

choices.english: I make lots of mistakes too!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يا هَلا! إِذاً نَحنُ سَواء! هَيّا نَغلَط مَعاً ونَتَعَلَّم مَعاً!
lines.english: Hey there! So we're the same! Let's make mistakes together and learn together!
lines.transliteration: ya halaa! idhan nahnu sawaa'! hayya naghlat ma'an wa nata'allam ma'an!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الشَّيخُ يوسُف يَقولُ: الغَلَطُ في التَّعَلُّم كَالسَّقطَةِ في المَشي — ضَرورِيَّة!
lines.english: Sheikh Yusuf says: mistakes in learning are like stumbling in walking — necessary!
lines.transliteration: ash-shaykh yuusuf yaquul: al-ghalat fit-ta'allum kas-saqta fil-mashi — daruurriyya!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العَرَبِيَّةُ سَهلَةٌ إذا لم تَخَفْ مِنَ الغَلَط. سَهل — هَذِهِ كَلِمَةٌ مُهِمَّة!
lines.english: Arabic is easy if you don't fear mistakes. Easy — that is an important word!
lines.transliteration: al-arabiyya sahla idha lam takhaf min al-ghalat. sahl — hadhihi kalimah muhimma!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل تَعرِفُ 'صَحيح'؟ تَعني correct. 'غَلَط' تَعني wrong. تَعَلَّمهُما!
lines.english: Do you know 'sahiih'? It means correct. 'Ghalat' means wrong. Learn both!
lines.transliteration: hal ta'rifu 'sahiih'? ta'nii correct. 'ghalat' ta'nii wrong. ta'allamahumaa!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يا هَلا! تَعَلَّمتُ شَيئاً مُذهِلاً اليَوم — لَيسَ في العَرَبِيَّةِ 'is' و 'am' و 'are'!
lines.english: Hey there! I learned something amazing today — Arabic has no 'is', 'am', or 'are'!
lines.transliteration: ya halaa! ta'allamtu shay'an mudhilan al-yawm — laysa fil-arabiyya 'is' wa 'am' wa 'are'!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بَدَلاً مِن 'I am a student' نَقول فَقَط 'أَنا طالِب'
lines.english: Instead of 'I am a student' we just say 'ana taalib'.
lines.transliteration: badalan min 'I am a student' naquul faqat 'ana taalib'
lines.culturalNote: Classical Arabic has no present-tense copula. The sentence 'al-bayt kabiir' (the house is big) has no verb — the meaning is carried purely by the juxtaposition. This is called a nominal sentence (jumla ismiyya).

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كَأَنَّكَ تَقول 'I, student.' بِدونِ فِعل! مُمتاز وَمُبَسَّط!
lines.english: It's as if you say 'I, student.' without a verb! Excellent and simplified!
lines.transliteration: ka'annaka taquul 'I, student.' bidooni fi'l! mumtaaz wa mubassit!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قُل مَعي: 'أَنا طالِب!' ثُمَّ 'الكِتابُ كَبير!'
lines.english: Say with me: 'Ana taalib!' Then 'al-kitaab kabiir!'
lines.transliteration: qul ma'ii: 'ana taalib!' thumma 'al-kitaab kabiir!'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: جَيِّد! كَبير — big! صَغير — small! هَذِهِ أَسهَلُ كَلِماتٍ في العَرَبِيَّة لأَنَّهُ لا يُوجَدُ فِعلٌ!
lines.english: Good! Kabiir — big! Saghiir — small! These are the easiest words in Arabic because there's no verb!
lines.transliteration: jayyid! kabiir — big! saghiir — small! haadhihi ashal kalimaat fil-arabiyya li'annahu laa yuujad fi'l!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يا هَلا! عِندي مُسابَقَة — هَيّا نَختَبِر!
lines.english: Hey there! I have a quiz — let's test it!
lines.transliteration: ya halaa! indii musaabaqaa — hayya nakhtabir!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا تَعَلَّمتُ دَرساً جَديداً اليَوم! تَعال نَتَذاكَر
lines.english: I learned a new lesson today! Come, let's review together.
lines.transliteration: ana ta'allamtu darsan jadiidan al-yawm! ta'aal natadhaakar

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أُستاذ يوسُف قال: المُراجَعَة أُمّ العِلم — ما رَأيُك؟
lines.english: Teacher Yusuf said: 'Review is the mother of knowledge' — what do you think?
lines.transliteration: ustaadh yuusuf qaal: al-muraaja'a umm al-'ilm — maa ra'yuk?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا كَثيراً ما أَنسى — لَكِن التَّكرار يُساعِد كَثيراً
lines.english: I often forget — but repetition helps a great deal.
lines.transliteration: ana kathiiran maa ansaa — laakin at-tikraar yusaa'id kathiiran

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: السَّلامُ عَلَيْكُم. أَنا حَمزَة، حارِسُ هَذا السُّوق
lines.english: Peace be upon you. I am Hamza, guard of this market.
lines.transliteration: as-salaamu alaykum. ana hamza, haarisu haadha as-suuq

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مُهِمَّتي حِراسَةُ السُّوق. لَكِنَّني أُحِبُّ الأَعدادَ أَيضاً
lines.english: My job is guarding the market. But I also love numbers.
lines.transliteration: muhimmatii hiraasatu as-suuq. laakinnanii uhibbu al-a'daada aydan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل تَعرِفُ الأَعدادَ بَعدَ العَشَرَة؟ لِنَبدَأ!
lines.english: Do you know the numbers after ten? Let us begin!
lines.transliteration: hal ta'rifu al-a'daada ba'da al-'ashara? linabda'!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحَدَ عَشَرَ — عَدَدُ اللّاعِبينَ في الفَريق
lines.english: Eleven -- the number of players on a team.
lines.transliteration: ahada 'ashara — adadu al-laa'ibiina fil-fariiq

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِثنا عَشَرَ — عَدَدُ الأَشهُرِ في السَّنَة
lines.english: Twelve -- the number of months in a year.
lines.transliteration: ithnaa 'ashara — adadu al-ashhuri fis-sana

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ثَلاثَةَ عَشَرَ — رَقَمٌ قَوِيّ!
lines.english: Thirteen -- a powerful number!
lines.transliteration: thalaathata 'ashara — raqamun qawii!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أُريدُ أَن أَرى قُوَّتَك في الأَعداد!
lines.english: I want to see your strength with numbers!
lines.transliteration: uriidu an araa quwwatak fil-a'daad!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهلاً. أَنتَ عُدتَ. جَيِّد. لِنُكمِل
lines.english: Hello. You are back. Good. Let us continue.
lines.transliteration: ahlan. anta udta. jayyid. linukmil

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَربَعَةَ عَشَرَ — عُمري عِندَما بَدَأتُ الحِراسَة
lines.english: Fourteen -- my age when I started guarding.
lines.transliteration: arba'ata 'ashara — umrii indamaa bada'tu al-hiraasa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: خَمسَةَ عَشَرَ — عَدَدُ الحُرّاسِ في السُّوق
lines.english: Fifteen -- the number of guards in the market.
lines.transliteration: khamsata 'ashara — adadu al-hurraasi fis-suuq

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بِكَم — سُؤالٌ مُهِمّ في السُّوق. يَعني 'ما السِّعر؟'
lines.english: How much -- an important question in the market. It means 'what is the price?'
lines.transliteration: bi-kam — su'aalun muhimm fis-suuq. ya'nii 'ma as-si'r?'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَيّا نَختَبِر ذاكِرَتَك
lines.english: Let us test your memory.
lines.transliteration: hayyaa nakhtabir dhakirataka

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحسَنت. الآن سَأُعَلِّمُكَ عِباراتٍ تَحتاجُها في السُّوق
lines.english: Well done. Now I will teach you phrases you need in the market.
lines.transliteration: ahsant. al-aan sa-u'allimuka ibaaraatin tahtaajuhaa fis-suuq

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أُريدُ — عِندَما تُريدُ شَيئاً مِنَ التّاجِر
lines.english: I want -- when you want something from the trader.
lines.transliteration: uriidu — indamaa turiidu shay'an min at-taajir

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لا أُريدُ — عِندَما لا تُريدُ شَيئاً. مُهِمَّة لِلمُساوَمَة
lines.english: I don't want -- when you don't want something. Important for bargaining.
lines.transliteration: laa uriidu — indamaa laa turiidu shay'an. muhimma lil-musaawama

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مِن فَضلِك — كَلِمَةُ الأَدَب. قُلها دائِماً
lines.english: Please -- a word of politeness. Always say it.
lines.transliteration: min fadlak — kalimatu al-adab. qulhaa daa'iman

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِمتِحانٌ أَخير. كُن قَوِيّاً!
lines.english: A final test. Be strong!
lines.transliteration: imtihaanun akhiir. kun qawiyyan!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قِف! ماذا تُريد؟
lines.english: Halt! What do you want?
lines.transliteration: qif! maadha turiid?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا أَحْمي الواحَة
lines.english: I protect the oasis.
lines.transliteration: ana ahmii al-waaha

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لا أَحَد يَدْخُل بِدونِ إِذْن
lines.english: No one enters without permission.
lines.transliteration: laa ahad yadkhul bidooni idhn

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحْتاجُ مُساعِد لِلدَّوْرِيَّة
lines.english: I need an assistant for the patrol.
lines.transliteration: ahtaaju musaa'id lid-dawriyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قُم بِدَوْرِيَّة حَوْلَ الواحَة
lines.english: Do a patrol around the oasis.
lines.transliteration: qum bi-dawriyya hawl al-waaha

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: رَأَيْتُ أَشياء غَريبَة في الصَّحْراء
lines.english: I have seen strange things in the desert.
lines.transliteration: ra'aytu ashyaa' ghariiba fis-sahraa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَصْوات... أَضْواء... لا أَعْرِف
lines.english: Sounds... lights... I don't know.
lines.transliteration: aswaat... adwaa'... laa a'rif

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قِف! أَنتَ عُدتَ. جَيِّد. الجُندِيُّ الجَيِّدُ يَعودُ دائِماً
lines.english: Halt! You returned. Good. A good soldier always returns.
lines.transliteration: qif! anta udta. jayyid. al-jundiyyu al-jayyid ya'uudu daa'iman

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أُعَلِّمُك كَلِمات المُحارِب. السَّيف — أَهَمُّ سِلاح
lines.english: I'll teach you warrior words. The sword — the most important weapon.
lines.transliteration: u'allimuk kalimaat al-muharib. as-sayf — ahamm silaah

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: القَوس وَالسَّهم — لِلمَسافَة البَعيدَة. الصَّبر — لِلمَسافَة الأَبعَد
lines.english: Bow and arrow — for long distance. Patience — for the longest distance.
lines.transliteration: al-qaws was-sahm — lil-masaafa al-ba'iida. as-sabr — lil-masaafa al-ab'ad

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: 'admiral' — كَلِمَة إنجليزيَّة مِن 'أَميرُ البَحر'. العَرَبُ كانوا أَسيادَ البَحر
lines.english: 'Admiral' — an English word from 'amir al-bahr'. Arabs were masters of the sea.
lines.transliteration: 'admiral' — kalima injiliziyya min 'amir al-bahr'. al-arab kaanu asiyaad al-bahr
lines.culturalNote: The word 'admiral' comes from Arabic 'amir al-bahr' (commander of the sea). Arab naval power reached its peak under the Fatimid and later the Ottoman Empire. The Mediterranean was an Arab sea for centuries.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: صَلاحُ الدِّين الأَيُّوبي — مِن أَعظَم القادَة. تَعَلَّمَ مِنَ الأَعداءِ وَانتَصَرَ
lines.english: Saladin — one of the greatest commanders. He learned from enemies and prevailed.
lines.transliteration: salaah ad-diin al-ayyuubii — min a'dham al-qaada. ta'allama min al-a'daa' wa intasar
lines.culturalNote: Saladin (Salah ad-Din, 1137-1193 CE) recaptured Jerusalem in 1187. He was renowned for his chivalry — he allowed Christian civilians to leave safely. Even his enemies, like Richard I, respected him.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عائِلَتي... أَنا أَعملُ بَعيداً. لَكِنَّهُم في قَلبي دائِماً
lines.english: My family... I work far away. But they are always in my heart.
lines.transliteration: aa'ilatii... ana a'mal ba'iidan. laakinnnahum fii qalbii daa'iman

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ابني... هُوَ في الثّامِنَة مِن عُمرِهِ. يُريدُ أَن يَكونَ حارِساً مِثلي
lines.english: My son... he is eight years old. He wants to be a guard like me.
lines.transliteration: ibnii... huwa fith-thaaminati min umurihi. yuriidu an yakuuna haarisan mithlii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قُلتُ لَهُ: أَوَّلاً تَعَلَّم! ثُمَّ اخدُم. الجُنديُّ الجاهِلُ خَطَر
lines.english: I told him: first learn! Then serve. An ignorant soldier is a danger.
lines.transliteration: qultu lahu: awwalan ta'allam! thumma ukhdum. al-jundiyyu al-jaahil khatar

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذا لِماذا أُعَلِّمُك الأَعداد — حَتّى لا تُخطِئَ في الحِساب يَوماً
lines.english: This is why I teach you numbers — so you don't make arithmetic errors someday.
lines.transliteration: haadhaa limaadha u'allimuk al-a'daad — hattaa laa tukhti' fil-hisaab yawman

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قِف! لَيسَ كُلُّ مَن يَأتي إلى البَوَّابَة صَديقاً
lines.english: Halt! Not everyone who comes to the gate is a friend.
lines.transliteration: qif! laysa kullu man ya'tii ilaa al-bawaaba sadiiqan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الحِصنُ — المَكانُ المَحمِيُّ. كَالقَلعَة لَكِن أَصغَر
lines.english: The fortress — a protected place. Like a castle but smaller.
lines.transliteration: al-hisn — al-makaan al-mahmiyyu. kal-qal'a laakin asghar
lines.culturalNote: Muslim military architecture reached its peak under Saladin. The Citadel of Cairo (built 1183 CE) used the same engineering principles as Crusader castles — in fact, Crusaders may have copied Muslim fortress designs.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الجُندِيُّ الجَيِّدُ لا يَحتاجُ سُيوفاً كَثيرَة — يَحتاجُ عَقلاً واحِداً صافِياً
lines.english: A good soldier doesn't need many swords — he needs one clear mind.
lines.transliteration: al-jundiyyu al-jayyid laa yahtaaju suyuufan kathiira — yahtaaju aqlan waahidan saafiyyan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قِف! ذاكَ يَكفي لِليَوم. عُدْ غَداً
lines.english: Halt! That's enough for today. Return tomorrow.
lines.transliteration: qif! dhaaka yakfii lil-yawm. ud ghadan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: المَدينَة مَحمِيَّة بِالأَسوار. تَعال أُريكَ
lines.english: The city is protected by walls. Come, let me show you.
lines.transliteration: al-madiina mahmiyya bil-aswaar. ta'aal uriika

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سور — الحائِط حَول المَدينَة. مِنهُ مَدينَة الصِّلاة السُّور في القُرآن
lines.english: Suur — the wall around a city. Also the name for Quran chapters (Sura).
lines.transliteration: suur — al-haa'it hawla al-madiina. minhu madiina
lines.culturalNote: The Arabic word "sura" (سورة), a Quran chapter, shares its root with "suur" (سور, wall). A sura is a section that stands complete on its own — like a walled enclosure that contains and protects what is within it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَلف حارِس حَرَسوا بَغداد في ذُروَتِها — أَعظَم مَدينَة في العالَم
lines.english: A thousand guards protected Baghdad at its peak — the greatest city in the world.
lines.transliteration: alf haaris harasuu baghdaad fii dhurwatihaa — a'zam madiina fil-'aalam

choices.english: Protecting the city is important! Thank you, Hamza.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلًا يَا صَدِيقِي! أَنَا عُمَرُ، المُزَارِعُ هُنَا.
lines.english: Hello my friend! I am Omar, the farmer here.
lines.transliteration: Ahlan ya sadiqi! Ana 'Umar, al-muzaari'u huna.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذِهِ الأَرْضُ طَيِّبَةٌ. الشَّمْسُ وَالمَطَرُ يَجْعَلَانِ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ يَنْمُو.
lines.english: This land is good. The sun and rain make everything grow.
lines.transliteration: Hadhihi al-ardu tayyibah. Ash-shamsu wal-mataru yaj'alani kulla shay'in yanmu.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَالَ، سَأُعَلِّمُكَ عَنِ الطَّبِيعَةِ. هَذِهِ هِيَ الشَّمْسُ.
lines.english: Come, I will teach you about nature. This is the sun.
lines.transliteration: Ta'aal, sa-u'allimuka 'an at-tabii'ah. Hadhihi hiya ash-shamsu.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: نَحْتَاجُ المَطَرَ لِلزِّرَاعَةِ. المَطَرُ نِعْمَةٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ.
lines.english: We need rain for farming. Rain is a blessing from God.
lines.transliteration: Nahtaaju al-matara liz-ziraa'ah. Al-mataru ni'matun min Allah.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اُنْظُرْ إِلَى تِلْكَ الشَّجَرَةِ الكَبِيرَةِ! زَرَعْتُهَا بِنَفْسِي.
lines.english: Look at that big tree! I planted it myself.
lines.transliteration: Undhur ila tilka ash-shajarah al-kabiirah! Zara'tuha bi-nafsi.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَيَّا نَرَى كَمْ تَعَلَّمْتَ عَنِ الطَّبِيعَةِ!
lines.english: Let's see how much you learned about nature!
lines.transliteration: Hayya nara kam ta'allamta 'an at-tabii'ah!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عُدْتَ! تَعَالَ أُرِيكَ حَيَوَانَاتِي.
lines.english: You're back! Come, let me show you my animals.
lines.transliteration: 'Udta! Ta'aal uriika hayawaanaati.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذَا هُوَ الجَمَلُ. هُوَ قَوِيٌّ وَصَبُورٌ فِي الصَّحْرَاءِ.
lines.english: This is the camel. He is strong and patient in the desert.
lines.transliteration: Hadha huwa al-jamalu. Huwa qawiyyun wa saburun fi as-sahraa'.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَهَذَا الحِصَانُ. هُوَ أَسْرَعُ حَيَوَانٍ فِي المَزْرَعَةِ!
lines.english: And this is the horse. He is the fastest animal on the farm!
lines.transliteration: Wa hadha al-hisaanu. Huwa asra'u hayawaanin fi al-mazra'ah!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الخَرُوفُ يُعْطِينَا الصُّوفَ الدَّافِئَ.
lines.english: The sheep gives us warm wool.
lines.transliteration: Al-kharuufu yu'tiina as-suuf ad-daafi'.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَالمَعْزَةُ تُعْطِينَا الحَلِيبَ اللَّذِيذَ!
lines.english: And the goat gives us delicious milk!
lines.transliteration: Wal-ma'zatu tu'tiina al-haliib al-ladhiidh!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: حَسَنًا، دَعْنَا نَخْتَبِرُ مَعْرِفَتَكَ بِالحَيَوَانَاتِ!
lines.english: Alright, let's test your knowledge of animals!
lines.transliteration: Hasanan, da'na nakhtabiru ma'rifataka bil-hayawaanaat!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَرْحَبًا مُجَدَّدًا! عِنْدِي حَيَوَانَاتٌ أُخْرَى لِتَتَعَلَّمَهَا.
lines.english: Welcome again! I have more animals for you to learn.
lines.transliteration: Marhaban mujaddadan! 'Indi hayawaanaatun ukhra li-tata'allamaha.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: البَقَرَةُ تُعْطِينَا الحَلِيبَ كُلَّ صَبَاحٍ.
lines.english: The cow gives us milk every morning.
lines.transliteration: Al-baqaratu tu'tiina al-haliib kulla sabaah.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الحِمَارُ يَحْمِلُ الأَشْيَاءَ الثَّقِيلَةَ. هُوَ صَدِيقُ المُزَارِعِ!
lines.english: The donkey carries heavy things. He is the farmer's friend!
lines.transliteration: Al-himaaru yahmilu al-ashyaa' ath-thaqiilah. Huwa sadiiqu al-muzaari'!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِسْمَعْ! ذَلِكَ صَوْتُ الطَّيْرِ فَوْقَ الشَّجَرَةِ.
lines.english: Listen! That is the sound of the bird above the tree.
lines.transliteration: Isma'! Dhaalika sawtu at-tayri fawqa ash-shajarah.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحْسَنْتَ! هَيَّا نَرَى إِنْ كُنْتَ تَذْكُرُ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ!
lines.english: Well done! Let's see if you remember everything!
lines.transliteration: Ahsanta! Hayya nara in kunta tadhkuru kulla shay'!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلاً وَسَهْلاً! الحَمْدُ لِلَّه على الحَصاد
lines.english: Welcome! Praise God for the harvest.
lines.transliteration: ahlan wa sahlan! al-hamdu lillaah ala al-hasaad

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الطَّبيعَةُ جَميلَة. دَعْني أُعَلِّمُك
lines.english: Nature is beautiful. Let me teach you.
lines.transliteration: at-tabii'a jamiila. da'nii u'allimuk

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: شَجَرَة — يَعني tree
lines.english: Shajara — means tree.
lines.transliteration: shajara — ya'nii tree

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الزِّراعَةُ في الواحَةِ قَديمَة جِدّاً
lines.english: Farming in the oasis is very ancient.
lines.transliteration: az-ziraa'a fil-waaha qadiima jiddan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَجْدادي زَرَعوا هُنا مُنْذُ مِئات السِّنين
lines.english: My ancestors farmed here for hundreds of years.
lines.transliteration: ajdaadii zara'uu hunaa mundhu mi'aat as-siniin

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الحَصادُ هَذا العام مُمتاز!
lines.english: This year's harvest is excellent!
lines.transliteration: al-hasaad haadhaa al-aam mumtaaz!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الأَمْطارُ جاءَت في الوَقْت المُناسِب
lines.english: The rains came at the right time.
lines.transliteration: al-amtaar jaa'at fil-waqt al-munaasib

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العَرَبُ أَحدَثوا ثَورَةً زِراعيَّة — الرَّي وَتَناوُبُ المَحاصيل
lines.english: Arabs created an agricultural revolution — irrigation and crop rotation
lines.transliteration: al-arab ahdathu thawra zira'iyya — ar-ray wa tanawub al-mahasil

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كَلِمَةُ 'قُطن' أَعطَت 'cotton' وَ'سُكَّر' أَعطَت 'sugar'
lines.english: 'Qutn' gave 'cotton' and 'sukkar' gave 'sugar'
lines.transliteration: kalimat 'qutn' a'tat 'cotton' wa 'sukkar' a'tat 'sugar'
lines.culturalNote: English borrowed extensively from Arabic through trade: cotton (qutn), sugar (sukkar), orange (naranj), lemon (laymun), lime (lima), artichoke (al-kharshuf).

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَ'نارَنج' أَعطَت 'orange' وَ'لَيمون' أَعطَت 'lemon'
lines.english: And 'naranj' gave 'orange' and 'laymun' gave 'lemon'
lines.transliteration: wa 'naranj' a'tat 'orange' wa 'laymun' a'tat 'lemon'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: حَتّى كَلِمَةُ 'الجَبر' أَصبَحَت 'algebra' وَ'صِفر' أَصبَحَت 'zero'
lines.english: Even 'al-jabr' became 'algebra' and 'sifr' became 'zero'
lines.transliteration: hatta kalimat 'al-jabr' asbahat 'algebra' wa 'sifr' asbahat 'zero'
lines.culturalNote: The concept of zero (sifr) was transmitted to Europe through Arabic mathematicians. The word 'cipher' also comes from sifr.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهلاً وَسَهلاً! الحَمدُ لِلَّهِ على الحَصاد. تَعالَ أُريكَ شَيئاً عَجيباً
lines.english: Welcome! Praise God for the harvest. Come let me show you something amazing.
lines.transliteration: ahlan wa sahlan! al-hamdu lillaah ala al-hasaad. ta'aala uriika shay'an ajiiban

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: القَناةُ — قَناةٌ مائِيَّةٌ تَحتَ الأَرض. أَجدادُنا بَنَوها منذُ آلاف السِّنين
lines.english: The qanat — an underground water channel. Our ancestors built them thousands of years ago.
lines.transliteration: al-qanaat — qanaat maa'iyya taht al-ard. ajdaaduna banawha mundhu aalaf as-siniin
lines.culturalNote: Qanats are ancient underground water channels that bring groundwater from aquifers to the surface by gravity. They were invented in Persia and spread across the Islamic world. Some are still functional after 3,000 years.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الماءُ يَسيرُ تَحتَ الأَرض مِيلاتٍ بِقوَّةِ الجاذِبِيَّة. لا مَضَخَّات! لا كَهرُباء!
lines.english: Water travels underground for miles by gravity. No pumps! No electricity!
lines.transliteration: al-maa' yasiiru taht al-ard miilaat bi-quwwat al-jaadhibiyya. laa madhakhkhaat! laa kahrubaa'!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الحَمدُ لِلَّه! هَذِهِ الواحَة تَعيشُ بِقَناةٍ بَناها جَدّي قَبلَ مِئَتَي سَنَة
lines.english: Praise God! This oasis lives by a qanat my grandfather built two hundred years ago.
lines.transliteration: al-hamdu lillaah! haadhihi al-waaha ta'iishu bi-qanaat banaahaa jaddii qabl mi'atay sana

choices.english: This is amazing! I want to learn

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهلاً وَسَهلاً! الحَمدُ لِلَّه! سَأُعَلِّمُكَ كَلِمات الأَرض
lines.english: Welcome! Praise God! I'll teach you the words of the earth.
lines.transliteration: ahlan wa sahlan! al-hamdu lillaah! sa-u'allimuka kalimaat al-ard

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَرض — هِيَ أُمُّ كُلِّ شَيء. مِنها نَأكُل وَإِلَيها نَعود
lines.english: Land — it is the mother of everything. From it we eat and to it we return.
lines.transliteration: ard — hiya ummu kull shay'. minhaa na'kul wa ilayhaa na'uud

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: زَرعَ — فِعلٌ مُقَدَّس. كُلُّ زَرعَةٍ صَدَقَة. هَكَذا قالَ النَّبيُّ عَلَيهِ السَّلام
lines.english: Planting — a sacred act. Every planted thing is charity. So the Prophet, peace be upon him, said.
lines.transliteration: zara'a — fi'lun muqaddas. kullu zar'atin sadaqa. haakadha qaala an-nabiyyu alayhis-salaam

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَالنَّخلَةُ — مَلِكَةُ الأَشجار في الصَّحراء. تُعطينا تَمراً وَظِلاً وَخَشَباً
lines.english: And the palm tree — queen of trees in the desert. It gives us dates, shade, and wood.
lines.transliteration: wan-nakhlatu — maliikat al-ashjaar fis-sahraa'. tu'tiinaa tamran wa dhillan wa khashaban

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: صَعبَة؟ الحَمدُ لِلَّه — كُلُّ حَياةٍ فيها صُعوبات. لَكِنَّ المُزارِعَ يَرى الثَّمَر
lines.english: Hard? Praise God — every life has difficulties. But the farmer sees the fruit.
lines.transliteration: sa'ba? al-hamdu lillaah — kullu hayaatin fiihaa su'uubaat. laakin al-muzaari' yaraa ath-thamar

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَزرَعُ اليَوم وَتَأكُلُ بَعدَ أَشهُر. الصَّبرُ هُوَ أَهَمُّ ما يَتَعَلَّمُهُ المُزارِع
lines.english: You plant today and eat after months. Patience is the most important thing a farmer learns.
lines.transliteration: tazra'u al-yawm wa ta'kulu ba'da ashhur. as-sabr huwa ahamm maa yata'allamuhu al-muzaari'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الحَمدُ لِلَّه على كُلِّ حَال — في الجَفاف وَفي المَطَر. هَذا ما عَلَّمَني أَبي
lines.english: Praise God in every situation — in drought and in rain. This is what my father taught me.
lines.transliteration: al-hamdu lillaah ala kull haal — fil-jafaaf wa fil-matar. haadhaa maa allamanii abii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهلاً! الحَمدُ لِلَّه! هَل تَعلَمُ عَن الثَّورَة الزِّراعيَّة في الأَندَلُس؟
lines.english: Welcome! Praise God! Do you know about the agricultural revolution in Andalusia?
lines.transliteration: ahlan! al-hamdu lillaah! hal ta'lamu an ath-thawra az-ziraa'iyya fil-andalus?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العَرَبُ أَدخَلوا إلى أُوروبَّا: البُرتُقال وَالقُطن وَالقَصَب وَالأَرُزَّ
lines.english: Arabs introduced to Europe: orange, cotton, sugarcane, and rice.
lines.transliteration: al-arab adkhalu ila urubba: al-burtuqaal wal-qutn wal-qasab wal-aruzz
lines.culturalNote: The Arab Agricultural Revolution (700-1100 CE) transformed Spain and Sicily. Arabs introduced irrigation, new crops, and crop rotation. Over 10,000 Arabic words entered Spanish, mostly through agriculture and science.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَنَشَروا نِظامَ السَّقي بِالرَّوافِع وَالسَّواقي — الأَرضُ الجافَّة صارَت خَضراء
lines.english: And they spread irrigation systems with water wheels and channels — dry land turned green.
lines.transliteration: wa nasharu nidhaam as-saqii bir-rawaafia was-sawaaqii — al-ard al-jaaffa saarat khadhraa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الحَمدُ لِلَّه! المُزارِعُ يَزرَعُ وَالأَرضُ تُعطي — هَذِهِ بَرَكَةُ العَمَل
lines.english: Praise God! The farmer plants and the earth gives — this is the blessing of work.
lines.transliteration: al-hamdu lillaah! al-muzaari' yazra'u wal-ard tu'tii — haadhihi barakat al-'amal

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ. أَنَا مَرْيَمُ، العَشَّابَةُ.
lines.english: Peace be upon you. I am Maryam, the herbalist.
lines.transliteration: As-salaamu 'alaykum. Ana Maryam, al-'ashshaabah.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أُدَاوِي النَّاسَ بِالأَعْشَابِ. لِذَلِكَ أَعْرِفُ أَجْزَاءَ الجِسْمِ جَيِّدًا.
lines.english: I heal people with herbs. That is why I know the body parts well.
lines.transliteration: Udaawi an-naasa bil-a'shaab. Li-dhaalika a'rifu ajzaa' al-jismi jayyidan.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لِنَبْدَأْ مِنَ الأَعْلَى. هَذَا هُوَ الرَّأْسُ.
lines.english: Let's start from the top. This is the head.
lines.transliteration: Li-nabda' min al-a'la. Hadha huwa ar-ra'su.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اليَدُ هِيَ أَدَاتُكَ لِجَمْعِ الأَعْشَابِ.
lines.english: The hand is your tool for gathering herbs.
lines.transliteration: Al-yadu hiya adaatuka li-jam'i al-a'shaab.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَالعَيْنُ تُسَاعِدُكَ عَلَى مَعْرِفَةِ النَّبَاتَاتِ الصَّحِيحَةِ.
lines.english: And the eye helps you identify the right plants.
lines.transliteration: Wal-'aynu tusaa'iduka 'ala ma'rifati an-nabaataat as-sahiihah.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: جَيِّدٌ! لِنَتَأَكَّدْ أَنَّكَ حَفِظْتَ هَذِهِ الكَلِمَاتِ.
lines.english: Good! Let's make sure you memorized these words.
lines.transliteration: Jayyid! Li-nata'akkad annaka hafidta hadhihi al-kalimaat.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عُدْتَ! الحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ. عِنْدِي المَزِيدُ لِأُعَلِّمَكَ.
lines.english: You're back! Thank God. I have more to teach you.
lines.transliteration: 'Udta! Al-hamdu lillah. 'Indi al-maziidu li-u'allimaka.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الأُذُنُ مُهِمَّةٌ. بِهَا نَسْمَعُ صَوْتَ الرِّيحِ فِي الأَشْجَارِ.
lines.english: The ear is important. With it we hear the sound of wind in the trees.
lines.transliteration: Al-udhunu muhimmah. Biha nasma'u sawta ar-riih fi al-ashjaar.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الفَمُ لِلْكَلَامِ وَالأَكْلِ. اِحْفَظْ هَذِهِ الكَلِمَةَ!
lines.english: The mouth is for speaking and eating. Remember this word!
lines.transliteration: Al-famu lil-kalaam wal-akl. Ihfadh hadhihi al-kalimah!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: القَلْبُ هُوَ مَرْكَزُ الحَيَاةِ. نَقُولُ: القَلْبُ السَّلِيمُ فِي الجِسْمِ السَّلِيمِ.
lines.english: The heart is the center of life. We say: a healthy heart in a healthy body.
lines.transliteration: Al-qalbu huwa markazu al-hayaah. Naquul: al-qalbu as-saliimu fi al-jismi as-saliim.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: البَطْنُ يَحْتَاجُ إِلَى طَعَامٍ صَحِّيٍّ. الأَعْشَابُ تُسَاعِدُ البَطْنَ!
lines.english: The stomach needs healthy food. Herbs help the stomach!
lines.transliteration: Al-batnu yahtaaju ila ta'aamin sihhiyy. Al-a'shaabu tusaa'idu al-batna!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مُمْتَازٌ! هَيَّا نَرَى كَمْ تَعْرِفُ الآنَ.
lines.english: Excellent! Let's see how much you know now.
lines.transliteration: Mumtaaz! Hayya nara kam ta'rifu al-aan.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَرْحَبًا! اليَوْمَ سَنَتَعَلَّمُ أَفْعَالًا مُهِمَّةً لِلْجِسْمِ.
lines.english: Welcome! Today we will learn important verbs for the body.
lines.transliteration: Marhaban! Al-yawma sanata'allamu af'aalan muhimmah lil-jism.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَكَلَ. الجِسْمُ يَحْتَاجُ أَنْ يَأْكُلَ طَعَامًا صَحِّيًّا كُلَّ يَوْمٍ.
lines.english: To eat. The body needs to eat healthy food every day.
lines.transliteration: Akala. Al-jismu yahtaaju an ya'kula ta'aaman sihhiyyan kulla yawm.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: شَرِبَ. اِشْرَبِ المَاءَ كَثِيرًا، خَاصَّةً فِي الحَرِّ!
lines.english: To drink. Drink water often, especially in the heat!
lines.transliteration: Shariba. Ishrabi al-maa'a kathiiran, khaassatan fi al-harr!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: نَامَ. النَّوْمُ الجَيِّدُ يَشْفِي الجِسْمَ مِثْلَ الأَعْشَابِ!
lines.english: To sleep. Good sleep heals the body like herbs!
lines.transliteration: Naama. An-nawmu al-jayyidu yashfi al-jisma mithla al-a'shaab!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحْسَنْتِ! لِنَخْتَبِرْ هَذِهِ الأَفْعَالَ.
lines.english: Well done! Let's test these verbs.
lines.transliteration: Ahsanti! Li-nakhtabir hadhihi al-af'aal.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلاً يا عَزيزي. الصِّحَّةُ تاج
lines.english: Welcome, dear. Health is a crown.
lines.transliteration: ahlan ya aziizii. as-sihha taaj

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كَيْفَ أُساعِدُك؟
lines.english: How can I help you?
lines.transliteration: kayfa usaa'iduk?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الجِسْمُ نِعْمَة مِنَ اللَّه. لِنَتَعَلَّم
lines.english: The body is a blessing from God. Let us learn.
lines.transliteration: al-jism ni'ma min allaah. linata'allam

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: رَأْس — هَذا head
lines.english: Ra's — this is the head.
lines.transliteration: ra's — haadhaa head

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يَد — هَذِهِ hand
lines.english: Yad — this is the hand.
lines.transliteration: yad — haadhihi hand

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الأَعْشابُ الطِّبِّيَّةُ مَوْجودَة في الواحَة
lines.english: Medicinal herbs are found in the oasis.
lines.transliteration: al-a'shaab at-tibbiyya mawjuuda fil-waaha

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كُلُّ نَباتٍ لَهُ فائِدَة
lines.english: Every plant has a benefit.
lines.transliteration: kull nabaat lahu faa'ida

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحْتاجُ مُساعَدَة في جَمْع الأَعْشاب
lines.english: I need help gathering herbs.
lines.transliteration: ahtaaju musaa'ada fii jam' al-a'shaab

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِجْمَع خَمْسَة أَنواع وَعُدْ إِلَيّ
lines.english: Gather five types and return to me.
lines.transliteration: ijma' khamsa anwaa' wa ud ilayya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِجْلِسْ، يا صَديقي. أُحَدِّثُكَ اليَومَ عَنِ الشَّيْخِ الرَّئيسِ ابنِ سينا.
lines.english: Sit, my friend. Today I will tell you about the Master Sheikh, Ibn Sina.
lines.transliteration: Ijlis, ya sadiiqi. Uhaddithuka al-yawma 'ani sh-shaykhi ar-ra'iis Ibn Siina.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كانَ ابنُ سينا طَبيبًا وَفَيلَسوفًا عاشَ في القَرنِ العاشِرِ الميلادي.
lines.english: Ibn Sina was a physician and philosopher who lived in the 10th century CE.
lines.transliteration: Kaana Ibn Siina tabiibanwa failasoofan 'aasha fil-qarni al-'aashiri al-miilaadiyi.
lines.culturalNote: Ibn Sina (Avicenna, 980-1037 CE) wrote the Canon of Medicine (al-Qanun fi al-Tibb), a medical encyclopedia that remained the primary medical textbook in European universities until the 17th century.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كِتابُهُ القانونُ في الطِّبِّ كانَ يُدَرَّسُ في جامِعاتِ أُوروبَّا لِسِتِّمائَةِ سَنَةٍ!
lines.english: His book, the Canon of Medicine, was taught in European universities for six hundred years!
lines.transliteration: Kitaabuhu al-Qaanun fi at-Tibb kaana yudarrasu fi jaami'aat Uroobba li-sittimi'ati sanah!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَكَلِمَةُ 'إكسير' في الإنجليزيَّةِ جاءَت مِنَ العَرَبيَّةِ: الإكسير.
lines.english: And the word 'elixir' in English came from Arabic: al-iksir.
lines.transliteration: Wa kalimat 'elixir' fil-injiliiziyyati jaa'at min al-'arabiyyah: al-iksir.
lines.culturalNote: The English word 'elixir' comes from Arabic 'al-iksir', itself from Greek 'xerion' (powder for wounds). Arab alchemists used it to describe miraculous healing substances, and the concept entered European medicine through Arabic translations.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَلَّمْنا 'نَظيف'. الجِسْمُ النَّظيفُ أَوَّلُ خُطْوَةٍ في الطِّبِّ.
lines.english: We learned 'clean'. A clean body is the first step in medicine.
lines.transliteration: Ta'allamnaa 'nadhiif'. Al-jismu an-nadhiifu awwalu khutwa fin-tibb.

choices.english: Tell me about the ancient hospitals

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَوَّلُ مُستَشفًى حَقيقيٍّ في العالَمِ كانَ في بَغداد سَنَةَ ثَمانِمائَةٍ وَعِشرينَ مِيلادِيَّة.
lines.english: The first real hospital in the world was in Baghdad in 820 CE.
lines.transliteration: Awwalu mustashfan haqiiqiyyin fil-'aalami kaana fi Baghdaad sanata thamaanmi'atin wa 'ishriina miilaadiiyyah.
lines.culturalNote: The Bimaristan (from Persian: 'place of the sick') was the Islamic world's hospital system. The Baghdad Bimaristan (820 CE) treated all patients free of charge, regardless of religion, race, or wealth — a revolutionary concept in medieval medicine.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كانَ البيمارِستانُ يُعالِجُ الجَميعَ مَجَّانًا: المُسلِمَ وَالمَسيحيَّ وَاليَهوديَّ وَالفَقيرَ.
lines.english: The bimaristan treated everyone for free: Muslim, Christian, Jew, and the poor.
lines.transliteration: Kaana al-biimaaristaanu yu'aaliju al-jamii'a majjaanan: al-muslima wal-masiihiyya wal-yahuudiyya wal-faqiir.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كانَ فيهِ أَطِبَّاءُ مُتَخَصِّصونَ: لِلعيونِ، وَلِلعَقلِ، وَلِلجِراحَة.
lines.english: It had specialized doctors: for eyes, for the mind, and for surgery.
lines.transliteration: Kaana fiihi atibbaa'u mutakhassisoon: lil-'uyooni, walil-'aqli, walil-jiraahah.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذا هو القَلبُ النَّابِضُ لِلحَضارَةِ الإسلامِيَّة — العِنايَةُ بِكُلِّ إنسان.
lines.english: This is the beating heart of Islamic civilization — caring for every person.
lines.transliteration: Haadha huwa al-qalbu an-naabidu lil-hadaarati al-islaamiyyah — al-'inaayatu bikulli insaan.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: طَيِّب، هَيَّا نَتَعَلَّمُ كَلِماتٍ لِلصِّحَّةِ وَالجِسم.
lines.english: Good, let us learn words for health and the body.
lines.transliteration: Tayyib, hayya nata'allamu kalimaat lis-sihha wal-jism.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اليَدُ — بِها نَجمَعُ الأَعشابَ وَنَشفي المَرضى.
lines.english: The hand — with it we gather herbs and heal the sick.
lines.transliteration: Al-yadu — biha najma'u al-a'shaaba wa nashfi al-mardaa.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العَيْنُ — بِها نَتَعَرَّفُ عَلى نَباتاتِ الشِّفاء.
lines.english: The eye — with it we recognize healing plants.
lines.transliteration: Al-'aynu — biha nata'arrafu 'ala nabaataat ash-shifaa'.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الرَّأسُ — إذا آلَمَ الرَّأسُ، جَرِّبْ زَيتَ الزَّيتون.
lines.english: The head — if the head aches, try olive oil.
lines.transliteration: Ar-ra'su — idhaa aalama ar-ra'su, jarrib zayta az-zaytoon.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عَظيم! لِنَختَبِرْ ما تَعَلَّمتَه.
lines.english: Excellent! Let us test what you have learned.
lines.transliteration: Addhiim! Li-nakhtabir maa ta'allamtah.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَرحَبًا يا عَزيزي. كَيفَ صِحَّتُك اليَوم؟
lines.english: Welcome, dear one. How is your health today?
lines.transliteration: Marhaban ya 'aziizi. Kayfa sihhhatuka al-yawm?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الصِّحَّةُ تاج عَلى رُؤوسِ الأَصِحَّاء. لا تَعرِفُ قيمَتَها إلا إذا مَرِضت.
lines.english: Health is a crown on the heads of the healthy. You only know its value when you fall ill.
lines.transliteration: As-sihha taaj 'ala ru'oosi al-asihha'. La ta'rifu qiimatahailla idhaa maridta.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنَا طَارِقٌ، شَيْخُ هَذَا المُخَيَّمِ.
lines.english: I am Tariq, the elder of this camp.
lines.transliteration: Ana Taariq, shaykhu hadha al-mukhayyam.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: فِي الصَّحْرَاءِ، نَقْرَأُ الوَقْتَ مِنَ النُّجُومِ وَالشَّمْسِ.
lines.english: In the desert, we read time from the stars and the sun.
lines.transliteration: Fi as-sahraa', naqra'u al-waqta min an-nujuum wash-shams.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَوَّلُ شَيْءٍ: اليَوْمُ. اليَوْمُ هُوَ هَدِيَّةٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ.
lines.english: The first thing: the day. The day is a gift from God.
lines.transliteration: Awwalu shay': al-yawmu. Al-yawmu huwa hadiyyatun min Allah.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَعِنْدَمَا تَغِيبُ الشَّمْسُ، يَأْتِي اللَّيْلُ بِنُجُومِهِ.
lines.english: And when the sun sets, the night comes with its stars.
lines.transliteration: Wa 'indama taghiibu ash-shamsu, ya'ti al-laylu bi-nujuumihi.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الصَّبَاحُ هُوَ أَجْمَلُ وَقْتٍ. الهَوَاءُ بَارِدٌ وَالنُّورُ جَمِيلٌ.
lines.english: The morning is the most beautiful time. The air is cool and the light is beautiful.
lines.transliteration: As-sabahu huwa ajmalu waqt. Al-hawaa' baaridun wan-nuuru jamiil.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: جَيِّدٌ. لِنَرَ إِنْ كُنْتَ تَفْهَمُ الوَقْتَ كَمَا نَفْهَمُهُ نَحْنُ.
lines.english: Good. Let's see if you understand time as we understand it.
lines.transliteration: Jayyid. Li-nara in kunta tafhamu al-waqta kama nafhamuhu nahnu.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عُدْتَ إِلَيْنَا. الصَّحْرَاءُ تُعَلِّمُنَا أَنَّ الوَقْتَ ثَمِينٌ.
lines.english: You have returned to us. The desert teaches us that time is precious.
lines.transliteration: 'Udta ilayna. As-sahraa'u tu'allimuna anna al-waqta thamiinun.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: المَسَاءُ هُوَ وَقْتُ الرَّاحَةِ وَالحِكَايَاتِ عِنْدَ النَّارِ.
lines.english: The evening is the time of rest and stories by the fire.
lines.transliteration: Al-masaa'u huwa waqtu ar-raahah wal-hikaayaat 'inda an-naar.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اليَوْمَ نَحْنُ هُنَا. هَذَا هُوَ اليَوْمُ — الآنَ، هَذِهِ اللَّحْظَةَ.
lines.english: Today we are here. This is today -- now, this moment.
lines.transliteration: Al-yawma nahnu huna. Hadha huwa al-yawm -- al-aan, hadhihi al-lahdhah.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: غَدًا سَنَرْحَلُ مَعَ الرِّيحِ. غَدًا دَائِمًا يَأْتِي.
lines.english: Tomorrow we will travel with the wind. Tomorrow always comes.
lines.transliteration: Ghadan sanarhalu ma'a ar-riih. Ghadan daa'iman ya'ti.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَمْسِ مَضَى وَلَنْ يَعُودَ. لَا تَنْدَمْ عَلَى أَمْسِ.
lines.english: Yesterday has passed and will not return. Do not regret yesterday.
lines.transliteration: Amsi mada wa lan ya'uud. La tandam 'ala amsi.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَلْ تَعْرِفُ الفَرْقَ بَيْنَ اليَوْمِ وَغَدٍ وَأَمْسِ؟ لِنَرَ!
lines.english: Do you know the difference between today, tomorrow, and yesterday? Let's see!
lines.transliteration: Hal ta'rifu al-farqa bayna al-yawmi wa ghadin wa amsi? Li-nara!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلًا! جِئْتَ فِي الوَقْتِ المُنَاسِبِ. عِنْدِي كَلِمَاتٌ جَدِيدَةٌ.
lines.english: Welcome! You came at the right time. I have new words.
lines.transliteration: Ahlan! Ji'ta fi al-waqti al-munaasib. 'Indi kalimaatun jadiidah.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: السَّاعَةُ تَقِيسُ الوَقْتَ. كَمْ سَاعَةً مَشَيْتَ فِي الصَّحْرَاءِ؟
lines.english: The hour measures time. How many hours did you walk in the desert?
lines.transliteration: As-saa'atu taqiisu al-waqt. Kam saa'atan mashayta fi as-sahraa'?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الأُسْبُوعُ فِيهِ سَبْعَةُ أَيَّامٍ. نَرْحَلُ كُلَّ أُسْبُوعٍ.
lines.english: The week has seven days. We travel every week.
lines.transliteration: Al-usbuu'u fiihi sab'atu ayyaam. Narhalu kulla usbuu'.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الشَّهْرُ يَبْدَأُ مَعَ القَمَرِ الجَدِيدِ. نَحْنُ نَتْبَعُ القَمَرَ.
lines.english: The month begins with the new moon. We follow the moon.
lines.transliteration: Ash-shahru yabda'u ma'a al-qamari al-jadiid. Nahnu natba'u al-qamar.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِخْتِبَارٌ أَخِيرٌ عَنِ الوَقْتِ. أَنْتَ جَاهِزٌ!
lines.english: A final test about time. You are ready!
lines.transliteration: Ikhtibaarun akhiir 'an al-waqt. Anta jaahiz!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: السَّلامُ عَلَيْكُم يا شاب. الحِكْمَةُ مَعَ التَّجْرِبَة
lines.english: Peace be upon you, young one. Wisdom comes with experience.
lines.transliteration: as-salaamu alaykum ya shaab. al-hikma ma'a at-tajriba

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الصَّحْرَاءُ مُعَلِّمَةٌ قَاسِيَةٌ لَكِنَّهَا عَادِلَةٌ.
lines.english: The desert is a harsh teacher, but a fair one.
lines.transliteration: As-sahraa'u mu'allimatun qaasiyatun laakinnaha 'aadilah.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تُعَلِّمُنَا الصَّبْرَ وَقِيمَةَ المَاءِ وَقِيمَةَ الوَقْتِ.
lines.english: It teaches us patience, the value of water, and the value of time.
lines.transliteration: Tu'allimuna as-sabra wa qiimata al-maa'i wa qiimata al-waqt.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِحْفَظْ هَذَا فِي قَلْبِكَ يَا صَدِيقِي.
lines.english: Keep this in your heart, my friend.
lines.transliteration: Ihfadh hadha fi qalbika ya sadiiqi.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذِهِ القَرْيَةُ قَديمَة جِدّاً
lines.english: This village is very ancient.
lines.transliteration: haadhihi al-qarya qadiima jiddan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا رَأَيْتُ تَسْعينَ عاماً هُنا
lines.english: I have seen ninety years here.
lines.transliteration: ana ra'aytu tis'iin aaman hunaa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَكانَ جَدّي هُنا قَبْلي
lines.english: And my grandfather was here before me.
lines.transliteration: wa kaana jaddii hunaa qablii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الحِكْمَةُ لا تَأتي بِسُهولَة
lines.english: Wisdom does not come easily.
lines.transliteration: al-hikma laa ta'tii bi-suhuula

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِذْهَب وَتَعَلَّم مِن كُلِّ أَهْل القَرْيَة
lines.english: Go and learn from all the village people.
lines.transliteration: idh-hab wa ta'allam min kull ahl al-qarya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الأَمْثالُ العَرَبِيَّةُ حِكْمَة الأَجْداد
lines.english: Arabic proverbs are the wisdom of ancestors.
lines.transliteration: al-amthaal al-arabiyya hikmat al-ajdaad

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَثَل: العِلْمُ نور
lines.english: Proverb: Knowledge is light.
lines.transliteration: mathal: al-ilmu nuur

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِجلِس يا صَديقي. أَنظُر إلى السَّماء — كُلُّ نَجمٍ لَهُ اسمٌ عَربيٌّ قَديم.
lines.english: Sit, my friend. Look at the sky — every star has an ancient Arabic name.
lines.transliteration: Ijlis ya sadiiqi. Undhur ila as-samaa' — kullu najmin lahu ismun 'arabiyyun qadiim.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: النَّجمُ الأَحمَرُ الكَبيرُ؟ اسمُهُ الدَّبَران — مَعناهُ 'التَّابِع'.
lines.english: That large red star? Its name is al-Dabaran — it means 'the follower'.
lines.transliteration: An-najmu al-ahmaru al-kabiiru? Ismuhu ad-Dabaraan — ma'naahu 'at-taabi'u'.
lines.culturalNote: The star Aldebaran (alpha Tauri) gets its name from Arabic 'al-Dabaran' meaning 'the follower', because it appears to follow the Pleiades across the sky. Roughly two-thirds of all named stars have Arabic names, a legacy of Islamic Golden Age astronomy.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَذاكَ النَّجمُ العَملاق؟ يَدُ الجَوزاء. بِالإنجليزيَّةِ يُسَمُّونَهُ 'بيتِلجوز'.
lines.english: And that giant star? Yad al-Jawza'. In English they call it 'Betelgeuse'.
lines.transliteration: Wa dhaakin-najmu al-'amlaaqu? Yadu al-Jawzaa'. Bil-injiliiziyyati yusammuunahu 'Betelgeuse'.
lines.culturalNote: Betelgeuse comes from Arabic 'yad al-jawza'' meaning 'the hand of Orion' (al-Jawza' was the Arabic name for the Orion constellation). The name was corrupted through medieval Latin transliteration from 'Ibṭ al-Jauzā'' (armpit of Orion).

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: النُّجومُ هِيَ خَريطَتُنا في الصَّحراء. الشَّمالُ دائِمًا عِندَ نَجمِ القُطب.
lines.english: The stars are our map in the desert. North is always at the Pole Star.
lines.transliteration: An-nujoomu hiya khariitatuna fis-sahraa'. Ash-shamalu daa'iman 'inda najm al-qutb.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: في الصَّحراءِ بِلا خَريطَةٍ، الجِهاتُ حَياتُكَ أو مَوتُكَ.
lines.english: In the desert without a map, the directions are your life or your death.
lines.transliteration: Fis-sahraa'i bilaa khariitatin, al-jihaatu hayatuka aw mawtuka.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الشَّمالُ — نَجمُ القُطب يُرشِدُك. الجَنوبُ — ظِلُّكَ في الظُّهرِ يُشيرُ إليه.
lines.english: North — the Pole Star guides you. South — your shadow at noon points to it.
lines.transliteration: Ash-shamalu — najm al-qutbi yurshiduka. Al-janoob — dhilluka fidh-dhuhri yushiiru ilayhi.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الشَّرقُ — مِن هُناكَ تَشرُقُ الشَّمسُ كُلَّ صَباح.
lines.english: East — from there the sun rises every morning.
lines.transliteration: Ash-sharqu — min hunaaka tashruku ash-shamsu kulla sabaah.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الغَربُ — إلى هُناكَ تَغرُبُ الشَّمسُ. الغُروبُ أَجمَلُ لَحظاتِ الصَّحراء.
lines.english: West — there the sun sets. Sunset is the most beautiful moment in the desert.
lines.transliteration: Al-gharbu — ila hunaaka taghrubu ash-shamsu. Al-ghuroob ajmalu lahdhaat as-sahraa'.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مُمتاز! هَيَّا نَختَبِرُ هَذِهِ الجِهات.
lines.english: Excellent! Let us now test these directions.
lines.transliteration: Mumtaaz! Hayya nakhtabiru hadhihi al-jihaat.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يا صَديقي، أَشارِكُكَ حِكمَةَ أَجدادي — اِسمَع بِقَلبِكَ لا بِأُذُنَيكَ.
lines.english: My friend, I share with you the wisdom of my ancestors — listen with your heart, not your ears.
lines.transliteration: Ya sadiiqi, usharikuka hikmat ajdaadii — isma' biqalbika laa bi-udhunayik.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَثَلٌ بَدَوِيٌّ: 'اِسأَلْ عَن الرَّفيقِ قَبلَ السَّفَر، وَعَنِ الجارِ قَبلَ الدَّار'.
lines.english: A Bedouin proverb: 'Ask about the companion before the journey, and about the neighbor before the house'.
lines.transliteration: Mathalun badawiyyun: 'Is'al 'an ar-rafiiqi qabla as-safar, wa 'an al-jaari qabla ad-daar'.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَمَثَلٌ آخَرُ: 'الصَّحراءُ لا تَرحَمُ الجاهِلَ، وَلا تَنسى الحَكيمَ'.
lines.english: And another proverb: 'The desert has no mercy on the ignorant, and does not forget the wise'.
lines.transliteration: Wa mathalun aakhar: 'As-sahraa'u la tarham al-jaahil, wa la tansa al-hakiim'.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قَديمًا، كانَ البَدَوِيُّ يَحفَظُ الألفَ نَجم. اليَومَ، احفَظ أَربَعَةَ كَلِمات.
lines.english: Long ago, a Bedouin memorized a thousand stars. Today, memorize four words.
lines.transliteration: Qadiiman, kaana al-badawiyyu yahfadhu al-alfa najm. Al-yawm, ihfadh arba'ata kalimaat.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلًا! أَنَا نُورٌ، الرَّاوِيَةُ. أَرْوِي القِصَصَ لِأَهْلِ المُخَيَّمِ.
lines.english: Hello! I am Noor, the storyteller. I tell stories for the people of the camp.
lines.transliteration: Ahlan! Ana Nuur, ar-raawiyah. Arwi al-qisas li-ahli al-mukhayyam.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: فِي قِصَصِي حَيَوَانَاتٌ كَبِيرَةٌ وَصَغِيرَةٌ. لِنَبْدَأْ!
lines.english: In my stories there are big and small animals. Let's begin!
lines.transliteration: Fi qisasi hayawaanaatun kabiiratun wa saghiiratun. Li-nabda'!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كَانَ هُنَاكَ أَسَدٌ كَبِيرٌ يَعِيشُ فِي الجَبَلِ. كَبِيرٌ يَعْنِي... ضَخْمٌ!
lines.english: There was a big lion living in the mountain. Big means... huge!
lines.transliteration: Kaana hunaaka asadun kabiirun ya'iishu fi al-jabal. Kabiirun ya'ni... dakhm!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَكَانَتْ هُنَاكَ نَمْلَةٌ صَغِيرَةٌ لَكِنَّهَا ذَكِيَّةٌ جِدًّا!
lines.english: And there was a small ant, but she was very smart!
lines.transliteration: Wa kaanat hunaaka namlatun saghiiratun laakinnaha dhakiyyatun jiddan!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الأَسَدُ كَانَ قَوِيًّا. لَكِنَّ القُوَّةَ لَيْسَتْ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ!
lines.english: The lion was strong. But strength is not everything!
lines.transliteration: Al-asadu kaana qawiyyan. Laakinna al-quwwata laysat kulla shay'!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَلْ أَعْجَبَتْكَ القِصَّةُ؟ لِنَرَ إِنْ كُنْتَ تَذْكُرُ الكَلِمَاتِ!
lines.english: Did you like the story? Let's see if you remember the words!
lines.transliteration: Hal a'jabatka al-qissah? Li-nara in kunta tadhkuru al-kalimaat!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عُدْتَ لِسَمَاعِ المَزِيدِ! عِنْدِي قِصَّةٌ أُخْرَى.
lines.english: You came back for more! I have another story.
lines.transliteration: 'Udta li-samaa'i al-maziid! 'Indi qissatun ukhra.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كَانَ هُنَاكَ أَرْنَبٌ سَرِيعٌ وَسُلَحْفَاةٌ بَطِيئَةٌ.
lines.english: There was a fast rabbit and a slow turtle.
lines.transliteration: Kaana hunaaka arnabun sarii'un wa sulahfaatun batii'ah.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سَرِيعٌ! الأَرْنَبُ يَرْكُضُ كَالرِّيحِ!
lines.english: Fast! The rabbit runs like the wind!
lines.transliteration: Sarii'! Al-arnabu yarkudu kar-riih!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بَطِيءٌ! السُّلَحْفَاةُ تَمْشِي بِبُطْءٍ، لَكِنَّهَا لَا تَتَوَقَّفُ.
lines.english: Slow! The turtle walks slowly, but she never stops.
lines.transliteration: Batii'! As-sulahfaatu tamshi bi-but', laakinnaha la tatawwaqaf.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: فِي النِّهَايَةِ، السُّلَحْفَاةُ فَازَتْ! كَانَتْ سَعِيدَةً جِدًّا!
lines.english: In the end, the turtle won! She was very happy!
lines.transliteration: Fi an-nihaayah, as-sulahfaatu faazat! Kaanat sa'iidatan jiddan!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَالأَرْنَبُ كَانَ حَزِينًا لِأَنَّهُ خَسِرَ.
lines.english: And the rabbit was sad because he lost.
lines.transliteration: Wal-arnabu kaana haziinan li-annahu khasir.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قِصَّةٌ جَمِيلَةٌ! هَلْ تَذْكُرُ الكَلِمَاتِ؟
lines.english: A beautiful story! Do you remember the words?
lines.transliteration: Qissatun jamiilah! Hal tadhkuru al-kalimaat?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلًا! عِنْدِي قِصَّةٌ أَخِيرَةٌ لَكَ.
lines.english: Hello! I have one last story for you.
lines.transliteration: Ahlan! 'Indi qissatun akhiiratun laka.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: فِي الصَّحْرَاءِ، النَّهَارُ حَارٌّ جِدًّا كَالنَّارِ.
lines.english: In the desert, the daytime is very hot like fire.
lines.transliteration: Fi as-sahraa', an-nahaaru haarrun jiddan kan-naar.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَاللَّيْلُ بَارِدٌ كَالمَاءِ. هَكَذَا هِيَ الصَّحْرَاءُ.
lines.english: And the night is cold like water. That is how the desert is.
lines.transliteration: Wal-laylu baaridun kal-maa'. Haakadha hiya as-sahraa'u.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بَعْضُ القِصَصِ سَهْلَةٌ وَبَعْضُهَا صَعْبَةٌ. لَكِنَّ كُلَّهَا جَمِيلَةٌ!
lines.english: Some stories are easy and some are difficult. But all of them are beautiful!
lines.transliteration: Ba'du al-qisas sahlatun wa ba'duha sa'bah. Laakinna kullaha jamiilah!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سَهْلٌ. هَذِهِ الكَلِمَةُ سَهْلَةٌ، أَلَيْسَ كَذَلِكَ؟
lines.english: Easy. This word is easy, isn't it?
lines.transliteration: Sahlun. Hadhihi al-kalimatu sahlatun, alaysa kadhaalik?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: صَعْبٌ. لَا تَقْلَقْ، مَعَ التَّدْرِيبِ كُلُّ شَيْءٍ يَصِيرُ سَهْلًا!
lines.english: Difficult. Don't worry, with practice everything becomes easy!
lines.transliteration: Sa'bun. La taqlaq, ma'a at-tadriib kullu shay'in yasiiru sahlan!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذَا آخِرُ اِخْتِبَارٍ! أَنْتَ مُسْتَعِدٌّ!
lines.english: This is the final test! You are ready!
lines.transliteration: Hadha aakhiru ikhtibaarr! Anta musta'idd!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلاً! يُحْكى أَنَّ اليَوْمَ يَوْمٌ جَميل لِلقِصَص
lines.english: Welcome! It is said that today is a beautiful day for stories.
lines.transliteration: ahlan! yuhkaa anna al-yawm yawmun jamiil lil-qisas

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أُحِبُّ أَنْ أَرْوِيَ القِصَصَ! وَعِنْدَنا نُصوصٌ لِلقِراءَة أَيْضًا
lines.english: I love telling stories! And we have reading passages too.
lines.transliteration: uḥibbu an arwiya al-qiṣaṣ! wa-ʿindanā nuṣūṣ li-l-qirāʾa ayḍan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: القِراءَةُ تُساعِدُكَ على تَعَلُّمِ كَيْفَ تَتَرابَطُ الكَلِمات
lines.english: Reading helps you learn how words connect together.
lines.transliteration: al-qirāʾa tusāʿiduka ʿalā taʿallum kayfa tatarābaṭ al-kalimāt

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: جَرِّبْ تَمارينَ القِراءَة مِن قائِمَةِ 'أَنْشِطَة' في قائِمَةِ الإيقاف
