lines.english: Try the reading exercises from 'Activities' in the pause menu.
lines.transliteration: jarrib tamārīn al-qirāʾa min qāʾimat 'anshiṭa' fī qāʾimat al-īqāf

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يُحْكى أَنَّ هُناكَ كَنْز قَديم مَدْفون في الصَّحْراء
lines.english: It is said that there is an ancient treasure buried in the desert.
lines.transliteration: yuhkaa anna hunaaka kanz qadiim madfuun fis-sahraa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: البَعْضُ يَقولُ إِنَّهُ ذَهَب، وَالبَعْضُ يَقولُ كُتُب
lines.english: Some say it's gold, and some say books.
lines.transliteration: al-ba'd yaquulu innahu dhahab, wal-ba'd yaquulu kutub

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لَكِنْ لا أَحَد وَجَدَهُ بَعْد
lines.english: But no one has found it yet.
lines.transliteration: laakin laa ahad wajadahu ba'd

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الكَلِماتُ الوَصْفِيَّةُ تَجْعَل القِصَص جَميلَة
lines.english: Descriptive words make stories beautiful.
lines.transliteration: al-kalimaat al-wasfiyya taj'al al-qisas jamiila

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كَبير — big، صَغير — small
lines.english: Kabiir — big, saghiir — small.
lines.transliteration: kabiir — big, saghiir — small

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سَمِعْتُ قِصَّة عَن تاجِر مِن بِلاد بَعيدَة
lines.english: I heard a story about a trader from faraway lands.
lines.transliteration: sami'tu qissa an taajir min bilaad ba'iida

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يَقولُ إِنَّ هُناكَ مُدُن مِن ذَهَب!
lines.english: He says there are cities of gold!
lines.transliteration: yaquulu inna hunaaka mudun min dhahab!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِسمَعْ! اِسمَعْ! سَأَحكي لَكَ عَن أَعظَمِ راوِيَةٍ في التَّاريخ — شَهرَزاد!
lines.english: Listen! Listen! I will tell you about the greatest storyteller in history — Scheherazade!
lines.transliteration: Isma'! Isma'! Sa-ahki laka 'an a'dhami raawiiyatin fit-taariikh — Shahrazaad!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كانَت شَهرَزادُ تَحكي قِصَّةً كُلَّ لَيلَةٍ لِتُنقِذَ حَياتَها. أَلفُ لَيلَةٍ وَلَيلَة!
lines.english: Scheherazade told a story every night to save her life. One Thousand and One Nights!
lines.transliteration: Kaanat Shahrazaadu tahki qissatan kulla laylatin li-tunqidha hayaatahaa. Alfu laylatin wa laylah!
lines.culturalNote: One Thousand and One Nights (Alf Layla wa Layla) is a collection of Middle Eastern folk tales compiled during the Islamic Golden Age. Stories like Sinbad the Sailor, Aladdin, and Ali Baba reflect real 9th-century trade routes across the Indian Ocean and Silk Road.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَقِصَّةُ السِّندِباد؟ السِّندِبادُ مُسافِرٌ شُجاعٌ — يَعني شُجاع، جَريء!
lines.english: And the story of Sinbad? Sinbad is a brave traveler — meaning brave, courageous!
lines.transliteration: Wa qissatu as-Sindibaad? As-Sindibaadu musaafirun shujaa' — ya'ni shujaa', jarii'!
lines.culturalNote: The name 'Sinbad' may derive from 'Sind-bad' meaning 'river of the Indus' in Persian/Sanskrit, reflecting the real Indian Ocean trade routes Arab merchants sailed. The Sinbad tales preserve genuine geographical knowledge of 9th-century maritime trade.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: القِصَصُ لَيسَت مُجَرَّدَ تَسليَة — هِيَ تاريخٌ وَجُغرافيا وَحِكمَة!
lines.english: Stories are not mere entertainment — they are history and geography and wisdom!
lines.transliteration: Al-qisasu laysat mujarrada tasliya — hiya taarikhun wa jughraafiya wa hikmah!

choices.english: Teach me descriptive words from the stories
Tell me more about One Thousand and One Nights

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: في كُلِّ قِصَّةٍ جَيِّدَةٍ، هُناكَ وَصفٌ رائِعٌ. دَعني أُعَلِّمَكَ!
lines.english: In every good story, there is wonderful description. Let me teach you!
lines.transliteration: Fi kulli qissatin jayyidatin, hunaaka wasfun raa'i'. Da'ni u'allimaka!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: جَديد — كَأَنَّ الصَّباحَ الجَديد يَفتَحُ بابًا جَديدًا لِكُلِّ مُسافِر.
lines.english: New — as if the new morning opens a new door for every traveler.
lines.transliteration: Jadiid — ka-anna as-sabaaha al-jadiida yaftahu baaban jadiidan li-kulli musaafir.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قَديم — القِصَصُ القَديمَةُ هِيَ الأَجمَل. مِثلُ الخَمرِ، تَزدادُ جَمالًا مَعَ الزَّمَن!
lines.english: Old — the old stories are the most beautiful. Like wine, they grow more beautiful with time!
lines.transliteration: Qadiim — al-qisasu al-qadiimatu hiya al-ajmal. Mithlu al-khamri, tazdaadu jamaalan ma'a az-zaman!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: طَويل — القِصَّةُ الطَّويلَةُ تَملَأُ اللَّيلَ بِأَكمَلِه!
lines.english: Long — a long story fills the entire night!
lines.transliteration: Tawiil — al-qissatu at-tawiilatu tamla'u al-layla bi-akmalihi!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قَصير — وَالقِصَّةُ القَصيرَةُ تَترُكُ شَوقًا لِلمَزيد!
lines.english: Short — and the short story leaves you longing for more!
lines.transliteration: Qasiir — wal-qissatu al-qasiiratu tatruqu shawqan lil-maziid!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الآنَ لِنَختَبِرُ الأَلوانَ وَالأَوصافَ التي تَعَلَّمتَها!
lines.english: Now let us test the colors and descriptions you have learned!
lines.transliteration: Al-aana li-nakhtabiru al-alwaan wal-awsaaf allati ta'allamtaha!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يُحكى أَنَّ السِّندِبادَ رَأى بَحرًا أَزرَقَ كالسَّماء يَلتَقي بِأَرضٍ خَضراءَ كَالزُّمُرُّد.
lines.english: It is said that Sinbad saw a sea blue as the sky meeting land green as emerald.
lines.transliteration: Yuhkaa anna as-Sindibaada ra'aa bahran azraqa kas-samaa' yaltaqi bi-ardin khadhraa'a kaz-zumuruud.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَرَأى صَحراءَ حَمراءَ تَحتَ شَمسٍ ذَهَبِيَّة — الأَلوانُ هِيَ لُغَةُ الجَمال!
lines.english: And he saw a red desert under a golden sun — colors are the language of beauty!
lines.transliteration: Wa ra'aa sahraa'a hamraa'a tahta shamsin dhahabiyyah — al-alwaanu hiya lughatu al-jamaal!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: فِي القِصَصِ العَظيمَة، كُلُّ لَونٍ لَهُ مَعنى. الأَحمَرُ لِلخَطَر، الأَزرَقُ لِلأَمَل.
lines.english: In great stories, every color has meaning. Red for danger, blue for hope.
lines.transliteration: Fil-qisasi al-'azhiimah, kullu lawning lahu ma'na. Al-ahmar lil-khatar, al-azraq lil-amal.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الآنَ أَنتَ تَعرِفُ سِرَّ الرَّاوي: اِستَخدِم الأَلوانَ وَالأَوصافَ لِتُحيِيَ القِصَّة!
lines.english: Now you know the storyteller's secret: use colors and descriptions to bring the story to life!
lines.transliteration: Al-aana anta ta'rifu sirra ar-raawi: istakhdim al-alwaana wal-awsaaf li-tuhyiya al-qissah!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا سَليم، مُرشِد هَذا الجَبَل
lines.english: I am Salim, guide of this mountain.
lines.transliteration: ana saliim, murshid haadha al-jabal

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عِشتُ هُنا سِنين طَويلَة. أَعرِفُ كُلَّ حَيَوان
lines.english: I have lived here many years. I know every animal.
lines.transliteration: ishtu hunaa siniin tawiila. a'rifu kulla hayawaan

choices.english: I want to know the place first

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اُنظُر إِلى السَّماء. هَل تَرى ذَلِك الطَّيْر الكَبير؟
lines.english: Look at the sky. Do you see that big bird?
lines.transliteration: unzur ila as-samaa'. hal taraa dhaalik at-tayr al-kabiir?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ذَلِكَ نِسْرٌ — مَلِكُ الطُّيور
lines.english: That is an eagle — king of the birds.
lines.transliteration: dhaalika nisrun — maliku at-tuyuur

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِنتَبِه! بَيْنَ الصُّخور تَعيشُ الحَيَّةٌ
lines.english: Be careful! Among the rocks lives the snake.
lines.transliteration: intabih! bayna as-sukhuur ta'iishu al-hayyatun

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَهُناكَ أَرْنَبٌ — سَريعٌ جِدّاً في القَفْز
lines.english: And there is a rabbit — very fast at jumping.
lines.transliteration: wa hunaaka arnabun — sarii'un jiddan fil-qafz

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ثَلاثَة حَيَوانات. هَل حَفِظتَها؟
lines.english: Three animals. Did you memorize them?
lines.transliteration: thalaathat hayawaanaat. hal hafidtahaa?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عُدتَ. جَيِّد. الجَبَل فيهِ حَيَوانات أَكثَر
lines.english: You returned. Good. The mountain has more animals.
lines.transliteration: udta. jayyid. al-jabal fiihi hayawaanaat akthar

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الأَسَدٌ — أَقْوى حَيَوان في الجَبَل
lines.english: The lion — the strongest animal in the mountain.
lines.transliteration: al-asadun — aqwaa hayawaan fil-jabal

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: النَّمْلَةٌ — صَغيرَة لَكِنَّها قَوِيَّة
lines.english: The ant — small but strong.
lines.transliteration: an-namlatun — saghiira laakinnaha qawiyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: القِطَّةٌ — تَعيشُ مَعَ النّاس في القَرْيَة
lines.english: The cat — lives with the people in the village.
lines.transliteration: al-qittatun — ta'iishu ma'a an-naas fil-qarya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الكَلْبٌ — يَحرُسُ البُيوت
lines.english: The dog — guards the houses.
lines.transliteration: al-kalbun — yahrusu al-buyuut

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَربَعَة حَيَوانات جَديدَة. اِختَبِر نَفسَك
lines.english: Four new animals. Test yourself.
lines.transliteration: arba'at hayawaanaat jadiida. ikhtabir nafsak

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الحَيَوانات لَها صِفات. لِنَتَعَلَّم بَعْض الصِّفات
lines.english: Animals have qualities. Let's learn some adjectives.
lines.transliteration: al-hayawaanaat lahaa sifaat. linata'allam ba'd as-sifaat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: جَدِيدٌ — مِثل الثَّلج الجَديد عَلى الجَبَل
lines.english: New — like the new snow on the mountain.
lines.transliteration: jadiidun — mithl ath-thalj al-jadiid ala al-jabal

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قَدِيمٌ — مِثل هَذِهِ الصُّخور القَديمَة
lines.english: Old — like these old rocks.
lines.transliteration: qadiimun — mithl haadhihi as-sukhuur al-qadiima

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: جَمِيلٌ — مِثل مَنظَر الجَبَل عِندَ الغُروب
lines.english: Beautiful — like the mountain view at sunset.
lines.transliteration: jamiilun — mithl manzar al-jabal inda al-ghuruub

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كَلِمات مُهِمَّة. هَيّا نَرى ماذا تَذكُر
lines.english: Important words. Let's see what you remember.
lines.transliteration: kalimaat muhimma. hayyaa naraa maadha tadhkur

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذِهِ قَرْيَة الجَبَل. مَكان هادِئ وَجَميل
lines.english: This is the mountain village. A quiet and beautiful place.
lines.transliteration: haadhihi qaryat al-jabal. makaan haadi' wa jamiil

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: زَهراء الحائِكَة تَصنَعُ أَجمَل الثِّياب
lines.english: Zahra the weaver makes the finest clothes.
lines.transliteration: zahraa' al-haa'ika tasna'u ajmal ath-thiyaab

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَخَديجَة المُعالِجَة تَعرِفُ كُلَّ الأَعشاب
lines.english: And Khadija the healer knows all the herbs.
lines.transliteration: wa khadiija al-mu'aalija ta'rifu kulla al-a'shaab

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلاً! أَنا سَليم، دَليلُكَ. اِتَّبِعْني
lines.english: Welcome! I am Salim, your guide. Follow me.
lines.transliteration: ahlan! ana saliim, daliiluk. ittabi'nii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الاِتِّجاهاتُ مُهِمَّة! دَعْني أُعَلِّمُك
lines.english: Directions are important! Let me teach you.
lines.transliteration: al-ittijahaat muhimma! da'nii u'allimuk

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يَمين — right، يَسار — left
lines.english: Yamiin — right, yasaar — left.
lines.transliteration: yamiin — right, yasaar — left

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَمام — front، خَلْف — behind
lines.english: Amaam — front, khalf — behind.
lines.transliteration: amaam — front, khalf — behind

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هُناكَ ثَمان مَناطِق في العالَم
lines.english: There are eight zones in the world.
lines.transliteration: hunaaka thamaan manaatiq fil-aalam

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الواحَة، المَكتَبَة، السُّوق، البَدْو، وَالمَزيد
lines.english: The oasis, the library, the market, the Bedouin camp, and more.
lines.transliteration: al-waaha, al-maktaba, as-suuq, al-badw, wal-maziid

choices.english: I want to visit them all

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحْتاجُ مُساعِد لِرَسْمِ خَريطَة المَنطَقَة
lines.english: I need an assistant to map the area.
lines.transliteration: ahtaaju musaa'id li-rasm khariitat al-mantaqa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: زُرْ كُلَّ المَناطِق وَعُدْ إِلَيّ
lines.english: Visit all the zones and return to me.
lines.transliteration: zur kull al-manaatiq wa ud ilayya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَال، أُرِيكَ سِرَّ المُلَّاحِين العَرَب: النُّجوم هِيَ خَريطَتُنا!
lines.english: Come, I show you the secret of Arab navigators: the stars are our map!
lines.transliteration: Ta'aal, uriika sirr al-mullaahin al-'Arab: an-nujuum hiya khaaritatunaa!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كَلِمَة "zenith" الإِنجليزِيَّة مِن العَرَبِيَّة "سَمت" — أَي الاتِّجَاه في السَّمَاء!
lines.english: The English "zenith" is from Arabic "samt" — meaning direction in the sky!
lines.transliteration: Kalima 'zenith' al-injliiziyya min al-'arabiyya 'samt' — ay al-ittijjah fii as-samaa'!
lines.culturalNote: "Zenith" comes from Arabic "samt" (سَمت, direction). "Nadir" comes from Arabic "nadhiir" (نَظير, opposite). Both entered European science through Arab astronomical texts of the 9th-12th centuries.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: نَجمُ الشِّمَال يَدُلُّنا على الشَّمَال دَائِماً. تَعَلَّم: الشَّمَال!
lines.english: The North Star always points north. Learn: ash-shamaal (north)!
lines.transliteration: Najm ash-shimaal yadullunaa 'alaa ash-shamaal daa'iman. Ta'allam: ash-shamaal!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَعَكسُه: الجَنوب! مِن الشَّمَال تَعرِف كُلَّ شَيء!
lines.english: And its opposite: south! From north you know everything!
lines.transliteration: Wa 'aksuh: al-januub! Min ash-shamaal ta'rif kull shay'!

choices.english: Who was the greatest Arab navigator?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مُمتاز! الجِهَات الأَربَع. الشَّمَال وَالجَنوب عَرَفتَهُمَا. الآن: الشَّرق!
lines.english: Excellent! Four directions. You know north and south. Now: east!
lines.transliteration: Mumtaaz! Al-jihaat al-arba'. Ash-shamaal wal-januub 'araftahumaa. Al-aan: ash-sharq!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الشَّرق: مَطلَع الشَّمس. الغَرب: مَغرِبُها. بَينَهُما حَيَاتُنا كُلُّها!
lines.english: East: sunrise. West: sunset. Between them is all of our lives!
lines.transliteration: Ash-sharq: matla' ash-shams. Al-gharb: maghribuhaa. Baynahumaa hayaatunaaa kulluhaa!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَالغَرب! مَغرِب الشَّمس، مَوطِن الأَنْدَلُس والمَغرِب العَظيم.
lines.english: And west! Where the sun sets, homeland of Andalusia and the great Maghreb.
lines.transliteration: Wa al-gharb! Maghrib ash-shams, mawtin al-Andalus wal-Maghrib al-'aziim.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَيَّا نَختَبِر! مَن يَعرِف الجِهَات لَن يَضِيع أَبَداً!
lines.english: Let's test! One who knows the directions will never be lost!
lines.transliteration: Hayya nakhtabir! Man ya'rif al-jihaat lan yadii' abadan!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحسَنتَ! الجِهَات عَلى طَرف لِسَانِك الآن. أَنتَ مُلَّاح حَقِيقِي!
lines.english: Well done! The directions are on the tip of your tongue now. You are a true navigator!
lines.transliteration: Ahsanta! Al-jihaat 'alaa taraf lisaanik al-aan. Anta mullaahin haqiiqi!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحمَد بن مَاجِد! شَيخُ البَحَّارَة العَرَب — كَتَبَ أَربَعين كِتَاباً في فُنون المَلَاحَة!
lines.english: Ahmad ibn Majid! Master of Arab sailors — he wrote forty books on the arts of navigation!
lines.transliteration: Ahmad ibn Maajid! Shaykh al-bahhaara al-'Arab — kataba arba'iina kitaaban fii funuun al-malaaha!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قِيلَ أَنَّهُ دَلَّ فَاسكو دا غَاما على طَريق الهِند عَام 1498. المَعرِفَة العَرَبِيَّة فَتَحَت البَحَار!
lines.english: It is said he guided Vasco da Gama to India in 1498. Arab knowledge opened the seas!
lines.transliteration: Qiila annahu dalla Vaasco da Gama 'alaa tariiq al-Hind 'aam 1498. Al-ma'rifa al-'arabiyya fatahat al-bihaar!
lines.culturalNote: Ahmad ibn Majid (c.1421-1500 CE), called "The Lion of the Sea" (Asad al-Bahr), wrote comprehensive guides to Indian Ocean navigation. His star charts and wind knowledge were unmatched in his era.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَتَعَلَّم: فَوق — لِأَنَّ النُّجوم دَائِماً فَوقَنا وَتَدُلُّنا على الطَّريق!
lines.english: And learn: above — because the stars are always above us guiding our path!
lines.transliteration: Wa ta'allam: fawqa — li-anna an-nujuum daa'iman fawqanaa wa tadullunaa 'alaa at-tariiq!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يَا صَاحِبي، قَبلَ أَيِّ رِحلَة في الجَبَل، اِحفَظ هَذِهِ القَوَاعِد الثَّلاث!
lines.english: My companion, before any mountain journey, memorize these three rules!
lines.transliteration: Yaa saahib, qabla ayyi rihla fil-jabal, ihfaz haadhihi al-qawaa'id ath-thalaath!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: القَاعِدَة الأولى: اُنظُر دَائِماً إِلى السَّمَاء. المَطَر في الجَبَل يَأتي بِلا إِنذَار!
lines.english: Rule one: always watch the sky. Mountain rain comes without warning!
lines.transliteration: Al-qaa'ida al-uulaa: unzur daa'iman ilaa as-samaa'. Al-matar fil-jabal ya'ti bilaa indhaar!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: القَاعِدَة الثَّانِيَة: اِعرِف اليَمين واليَسَار دَائِماً. التَّرَدُّد في الجَبَل خَطير!
lines.english: Rule two: always know right and left. Hesitation in the mountains is dangerous!
lines.transliteration: Al-qaa'ida ath-thaaniya: i'rif al-yamiin wal-yasaar daa'iman. At-taraddud fil-jabal khatir!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: القَاعِدَة الثَّالِثَة: الرِّيح تُخبِرُكَ بِكُلِّ شَيء — اِستَمِع لِلرِّيح!
lines.english: Rule three: the wind tells you everything — listen to the wind!
lines.transliteration: Al-qaa'ida ath-thaalitha: ar-riyaah tukhbiruka bi-kulli shay' — ista'mil lir-riyaah!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِذهَب الآن — لَكِن كُن حَذِراً! الطَّريقُ يَنتَظِرُكَ وَأَنا هُنا دَائِماً.
lines.english: Go now — but be careful! The path awaits you and I am always here.
lines.transliteration: Idh-hab al-aan — laakin kun hadiran! At-tariiq yantaziruk wa ana hunaa daa'iman.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا خَديجَة. أُعالِجُ النّاس بِالأَعشاب مُنذُ سَنَوات طَويلَة
lines.english: I am Khadija. I have been treating people with herbs for many long years.
lines.transliteration: ana khadiija. u'aaliju an-naas bil-a'shaab mundhu sanawaat tawiila

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لِكَي تَفهَم الطِّبّ، يَجِب أَن تَعرِف الصِّفات
lines.english: To understand medicine, you must know adjectives.
lines.transliteration: likay tafham at-tibb, yajib an ta'rif as-sifaat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عِندَما يَأتي مَريض، أَسأَلُهُ عَن حالِه. لِنَبدَأ
lines.english: When a patient comes, I ask about their condition. Let's begin.
lines.transliteration: indamaa ya'tii mariid, as'aluhu an haalihi. linabda'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: نَظِيفٌ — الجُرح يَجِب أَن يَكون نَظيفاً
lines.english: Clean — the wound must be clean.
lines.transliteration: naziifun — al-jurh yajib an yakuuna naziifan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَسِخٌ — إِذا كانَ وَسِخاً، يُصبِح أَسوَأ
lines.english: Dirty — if it is dirty, it gets worse.
lines.transliteration: wasikhun — idhaa kaana wasikhan, yusbihu aswa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قَوِيٌّ — الجِسم القَوِيّ يُشفى بِسُرعَة
lines.english: Strong — a strong body heals quickly.
lines.transliteration: qawiyyun — al-jism al-qawiyy yushfaa bisur'a

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: جَيِّد. هَل فَهِمتَ هَذِهِ الصِّفات؟
lines.english: Good. Did you understand these adjectives?
lines.transliteration: jayyid. hal fahimta haadhihi as-sifaat?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلاً يا بُنَيّ. لِنُكمِل دَرسَنا في الصِّفات
lines.english: Welcome, dear child. Let's continue our lesson in adjectives.
lines.transliteration: ahlan ya bunayy. linukmil darsanaa fis-sifaat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ضَعِيفٌ — عَكس قَوِيّ. المَريض يَكون ضَعيفاً
lines.english: Weak — the opposite of strong. The sick person is weak.
lines.transliteration: da'iifun — aks qawiyy. al-mariid yakuun da'iifan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: طَوِيلٌ — الشَّجَرَة طَويلَة فيها أَعشاب مُفيدَة
lines.english: Tall/Long — the tall tree has useful herbs.
lines.transliteration: tawiilun — ash-shajara tawiila fiihaa a'shaab mufiida

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قَصِيرٌ — الأَعشاب القَصيرَة قَريبَة مِن الأَرض
lines.english: Short — the short herbs are close to the ground.
lines.transliteration: qasiirun — al-a'shaab al-qasiira qariiba min al-ard

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قَبِيحٌ — بَعض الأَدوِيَة طَعمُها قَبيح لَكِنَّها مُفيدَة
lines.english: Ugly/Unpleasant — some medicines taste bad but they are useful.
lines.transliteration: qabiihun — ba'd al-adwiya ta'muhaa qabiih laakinnaha mufiida

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَربَع صِفات جَديدَة. لِنَرى ماذا تَذكُر
lines.english: Four new adjectives. Let's see what you remember.
lines.transliteration: arba' sifaat jadiida. linaraa maadha tadhkur

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنتَ تَتَقَدَّم. اليَوم نَتَعَلَّم شَيئاً مُختَلِفاً
lines.english: You are progressing. Today we learn something different.
lines.transliteration: anta tataqaddam. al-yawm nata'allam shay'an mukhtalifan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: جَوَارِب — تَحمي القَدَمَين مِن البَرد
lines.english: Socks — protect the feet from the cold.
lines.transliteration: jawaarib — tahmii al-qadamayn min al-bard

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: نَظَّارَات — تُساعِد العُيون الضَّعيفَة
lines.english: Glasses — help weak eyes.
lines.transliteration: nazzaaraat — tusaa'id al-uyuun ad-da'iifa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سَعِيدٌ — الإِنسان السَّعيد يَشفى أَسرَع
lines.english: Happy — a happy person heals faster.
lines.transliteration: sa'iidun — al-insaan as-sa'iid yashfaa asra'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مُمتاز! هَيّا نَختَبِر كُلّ ما تَعَلَّمتَ
lines.english: Excellent! Let's test everything you learned.
lines.transliteration: mumtaaz! hayyaa nakhtabir kulla maa ta'allamta

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الأَعشاب هِيَ دَواء الطَّبيعَة. كُلّ عُشبَة لَها فائِدَة
lines.english: Herbs are nature's medicine. Every herb has a benefit.
lines.transliteration: al-a'shaab hiya dawaa' at-tabii'a. kullu ushba lahaa faa'ida

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لَكِن أَوَّلاً يَجِب أَن تَعرِف الصِّفات لِتَصِف الأَعراض
lines.english: But first you must know adjectives to describe symptoms.
lines.transliteration: laakin awwalan yajib an ta'rif as-sifaat litasif al-a'raad

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلاً يا بُنَيّ. بِالشِّفاء إِن شاء الله
lines.english: Hello, dear child. May healing come, God willing.
lines.transliteration: ahlan ya bunayy. bish-shifaa' in shaa' allaah

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كَيفَ أُساعِدُك اليَوم؟
lines.english: How can I help you today?
lines.transliteration: kayfa usaa'iduk al-yawm?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الجِسمُ أَمانَة. لِنَتَعَلَّم أَجزاءَهُ
lines.english: The body is a trust. Let us learn its parts.
lines.transliteration: al-jismu amaana. linata'allam ajzaa'ahu

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: رَأْسٌ — يَحمِلُ العَقل
lines.english: Head — it carries the mind.
lines.transliteration: ra'sun — yahmilu al-'aql

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يَدٌ — بِها نَلمِسُ وَنُشفي
lines.english: Hand — with it we touch and heal.
lines.transliteration: yadun — bihaa nalmisu wa nushfii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عَيْنٌ — تَرى الدَّواء وَالمَرَض
lines.english: Eye — it sees medicine and illness.
lines.transliteration: 'aynun — taraa ad-dawaa' wal-marad

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحسَنت! تَعَلَّمتَ ثَلاثَ كَلِمات
lines.english: Well done! You learned three words.
lines.transliteration: ahsant! ta'allamta thalaath kalimaat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الطِّبُّ العَرَبِيّ قَديم جِدّاً
lines.english: Arab medicine is very ancient.
lines.transliteration: at-tibbu al-'arabiyy qadiim jiddan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَجدادُنا اِستَخدَموا النَّعناع لِلمَعِدَة وَالبابونَج لِلنَّوم
lines.english: Our ancestors used mint for the stomach and chamomile for sleep.
lines.transliteration: ajdaadunaa istakhdamuu an-na'naa' lil-ma'ida wal-baabunaj lin-nawm

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كُلُّ عُشبَة فيها حِكمَة مِن الله
lines.english: Every herb contains wisdom from God.
lines.transliteration: kullu 'ushba fiihaa hikma min allaah

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَأَنا أُحاوِل أَن أُعَلِّم هَذِهِ الحِكمَة لِلجيل الجَديد
lines.english: And I try to teach this wisdom to the new generation.
lines.transliteration: wa ana uhaawilu an u'allima haadhihi al-hikma lil-jiil al-jadiid

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل سَمِعت؟ الحَدّاد داوود يَشكو مِن ظَهرِه
lines.english: Have you heard? Blacksmith Daud complains about his back.
lines.transliteration: hal sami't? al-haddaad daawuud yashkuu min zahrihi

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قُلتُ لَهُ: اِشرَب شاي الزَّنجَبيل كُلّ صَباح
lines.english: I told him: drink ginger tea every morning.
lines.transliteration: qultu lahu: ishrab shaay az-zanjabiil kulla sabaah

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَالأَميرَة عائِشَة طَلَبَت مِنّي أَعشاباً لِلنَّوم
lines.english: And Princess Aisha asked me for herbs for sleep.
lines.transliteration: wal-amiira 'aa'isha talabat minnii a'shaaban lin-nawm

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ابنُ سينا كَتَبَ القانونَ في الطِّبّ — أَعظَمُ كِتابٍ طِبّي
lines.english: Ibn Sina wrote the Canon of Medicine — the greatest medical text
lines.transliteration: ibn sina kataba al-qanun fit-tibb — a'zam kitab tibbi
lines.culturalNote: Ibn Sina's (Avicenna, 980-1037 CE) Canon of Medicine was used as a textbook in European universities until the 17th century — over 600 years.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: البيمارِستان — المُستَشفى — اختِراعٌ عَرَبي
lines.english: The bimaristan — the hospital — is an Arab invention
lines.transliteration: al-bimaristan — al-mustashfa — ikhtira' arabi
lines.culturalNote: The first hospitals (bimaristans) were established in Baghdad in the 9th century. They were free, treated all patients regardless of religion, and had separate wards for different conditions.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الرّازي فَرَّقَ بَينَ الحَصبَة وَالجُدَري أَوَّلَ مَرَّة
lines.english: Al-Razi distinguished between measles and smallpox for the first time
lines.transliteration: ar-razi farraqa bayna al-hasba wal-judari awwal marra

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: جَلَس، أُرِيدُ أَن أُحَدِّثَكَ عَن عَظِيم مِن أَطِبَّاء الإِسلَام: ابن النَّفيس.
lines.english: Sit, I want to tell you about a great Muslim physician: Ibn al-Nafis.
lines.transliteration: Jalis, uriiду an uhaddithak 'an 'aziim min atibba' al-islaam: Ibn an-Nafis.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: في القَرنِ الثَّالِثَ عَشَر، اِكتَشَفَ ابن النَّفيس الدَّورَة الرِّئَوِيَّة — قَبلَ هَارفَي بِثَلاثِمِائَة سَنَة!
lines.english: In the 13th century, Ibn al-Nafis discovered pulmonary circulation — 300 years before Harvey!
lines.transliteration: Fil-qarn ath-thaalith 'ashar, iktashafa Ibn an-Nafis ad-dawra ar-ri'awiyya — qabla Harvey bi-thalathimi'at sana!
lines.culturalNote: Ibn al-Nafis (1213-1288 CE) discovered that blood flows through the lungs (pulmonary circulation), not through the heart septum as Galen claimed. This was rediscovered in Europe by William Harvey in 1628 — 300 years later.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قَال: الدَّم يَمُرُّ عَبرَ الرِّئَة لا عَبرَ القَلب مُبَاشَرَةً. كَانَ مُحِقاً تَماماً!
lines.english: He said: blood passes through the lungs, not directly through the heart. He was completely right!
lines.transliteration: Qaala: ad-dam yamurr 'abra ar-ri'a laa 'abra al-qalb mubaasharatan. Kaana muhiqqqan tamааman!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَلَّم: القَلب — هُوَ مَركَز الحَيَاة. اِعتَنِ بِقَلبِك دَائِماً!
lines.english: Learn: the heart — it is the center of life. Always take care of your heart!
lines.transliteration: Ta'allam: al-qalb — huwa markaz al-hayaah. I'tani bi-qalbik daa'iman!

choices.english: What do you know about Arabic medicine?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بِكُلِّ سُرور! الجِسم هُوَ أَعظَم كِتَاب. لِنَبدَأ مِن الرَّأس.
lines.english: With pleasure! The body is the greatest book. Let us begin from the head.
lines.transliteration: Bi-kulli suruur! Al-jism huwa a'zam kitaab. Li-nabda' min ar-ra's.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الرَّأس — مَقَرُّ العَقل. العَقل هُوَ أَغلى ما تَملِك!
lines.english: The head — dwelling of the mind. The mind is the most precious thing you own!
lines.transliteration: Ar-ra's — maqarr al-'aql. Al-'aql huwa aghlaa maa tamlik!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العَين — بِها تَرى جَمَال العَالَم. اِحفَظها بِالنَّوم الكَافي!
lines.english: The eye — with it you see the beauty of the world. Guard it with sufficient sleep!
lines.transliteration: Al-'ayn — bihaa taraa jamaal al-'aalam. Ihfazhaa bin-nawm al-kaafi!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الأُذُن — بِها تَسمَع. وَالطَّبيب يَسمَع دَائِماً قَبلَ أَن يَتَكَلَّم!
lines.english: The ear — with it you hear. And a physician always listens before speaking!
lines.transliteration: Al-udhun — bihaa tasma'. Wa at-tabiib yasma' daa'iman qabla an yatakallam!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحسَنتَ! الجِسم هُوَ أَمَانَة الله عِندَكَ — اِعتَنِ بِه كَمَا تَعتَني بِحَديقَتِك.
lines.english: Well done! The body is God's trust with you — tend to it as you tend your garden.
lines.transliteration: Ahsanta! Al-jism huwa amaana Allaah 'indak — i'tani bihi kamaa ta'tani bi-hadiigatik.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الطِّبُّ العَرَبي! ابن سِينا كَتَبَ "القَانون في الطِّبّ" — المَرجِع الطِّبِّيّ في أُوروبَّا لِسِتِّمِائَة سَنَة!
lines.english: Arabic medicine! Ibn Sina wrote "The Canon of Medicine" — the medical reference in Europe for 600 years!
lines.transliteration: At-tibb al-'arabi! Ibn Sina kataba 'Al-Qaanuun fit-Tibb' — al-marja' at-tibbiyy fii Uurubba li-sittimi'at sana!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كَلِمَة "syrup" الإِنجليزِيَّة مِن العَرَبِيَّة "شَرَاب" — الدَّواء الحُلو!
lines.english: The English word "syrup" comes from Arabic "sharaab" — the sweet medicine!
lines.transliteration: Kalima 'syrup' al-injliiziyya min al-'arabiyya 'sharaab' — ad-dawaa' al-hulw!
lines.culturalNote: "Syrup" comes from Arabic "sharaab" (شَرَاب, drink/potion). "Camphor" comes from Arabic "kafuur" (كَافور). "Alcohol" comes from Arabic "al-kuhl" (الكُحل, the kohl/essence). Arab pharmacists invented distillation and modern drug preparation.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَكَلِمَة "camphor" مِن "كَافور". الأَطِبَّاء العَرَب أَعطَوا العَالَم ثَمَانِيَة أَعشَار عِلم الصَّيدَلَة!
lines.english: And "camphor" from "kafuur." Arab physicians gave the world eight-tenths of pharmacy!
lines.transliteration: Wa kalima 'camphor' min 'kaafuur'. Al-atibba' al-'Arab a'taw al-'aalam thamaaniyat a'shaarin 'ilm as-saydala!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَلَّم: الفَم — بِه تَأكُل وَتَتَكَلَّم. اِحفَظه بِالسِّواك!
lines.english: Learn: the mouth — with it you eat and speak. Guard it with siwak!
lines.transliteration: Ta'allam: al-fam — bihi ta'kul wa tatakallam. Ihfazh bis-siwaak!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا الإِمامُ مُحَمَّد، أُعَلِّمُ فِي مَكْتَبَةِ القَصْر
lines.english: I am Imam Muhammad. I teach in the palace library.
lines.transliteration: ana al-imaamu muhammad, u'allimu fii maktabati al-qasr

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سَمِعْتُ أَنَّكَ قَطَعْتَ رِحْلَةً طَوِيلَةً لِتَصِلَ إِلى هُنا
lines.english: I heard that you made a long journey to reach here.
lines.transliteration: sami'tu annaka qata'ta rihlatan tawiila litasila ilaa hunaa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اَلْعِلْمُ نُورٌ. وَأَنتَ حَمَلْتَ هَذا النُّورَ مَعَكَ طُولَ الطَّرِيق
lines.english: Knowledge is light. And you have carried this light with you the whole way.
lines.transliteration: al-ilmu nuur. wa anta hamalta haadha an-nuura ma'aka tuula at-tariiq

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: دَعْنِي أُعَلِّمُكَ أَفْعالَ العِلْمِ — أَهَمُّ الأَفْعالِ فِي حَياتِنا
lines.english: Let me teach you the verbs of knowledge — the most important verbs in our lives.
lines.transliteration: da'nii u'allimuka af'aala al-ilmi — ahammu al-af'aali fii hayaatinaa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّه. لِنَبْدَأ بِأَفْعالِ العِلْم
lines.english: In the name of God. Let us begin with the verbs of knowledge.
lines.transliteration: bismillaah. linabda' bi-af'aali al-ilm

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قَرَأَ — أَوَّلُ كَلِمَةٍ نَزَلَتْ مِنَ السَّماء
lines.english: Qara'a — the first word that came down from the heavens.
lines.transliteration: qara'a — awwalu kalimatin nazalat min as-samaa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كَتَبَ — بِالقَلَمِ يُحْفَظُ العِلْم
lines.english: Kataba — with the pen, knowledge is preserved.
lines.transliteration: kataba — bil-qalami yuhfazu al-ilm

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَلَّمَ — وَهَذا ما تَفْعَلُهُ أَنتَ الآن
lines.english: Ta'allama — and this is what you are doing right now.
lines.transliteration: ta'allama — wa haadha maa taf'aluhu anta al-aan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذِهِ أَساسُ كُلِّ عِلْم. لِنَرَ إِنْ فَهِمْتَ
lines.english: These are the foundation of all knowledge. Let us see if you understood.
lines.transliteration: haadhihi asaasu kulli ilm. linara in fahimta

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّه، عُدْتَ لِلتَّعَلُّم. لَدَيَّ أَفْعالٌ جَدِيدَة
lines.english: Thank God, you returned to learn. I have new verbs.
lines.transliteration: al-hamdu lillaah, udta lit-ta'allum. ladayya af'aalun jadiida

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عَرَفَ — العِلْمُ يَبْدَأُ بِالمَعْرِفَة
lines.english: Arafa — knowledge begins with knowing.
lines.transliteration: arafa — al-ilmu yabda'u bil-ma'rifa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَعْطى — خَيْرُ النّاسِ مَنْ يُعْطِي
lines.english: A'taa — the best of people are those who give.
lines.transliteration: a'taa — khayru an-naasi man yu'tii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ساعَدَ — وَالمُؤْمِنُ يُساعِدُ أَخاه
lines.english: Saa'ada — and the believer helps his brother.
lines.transliteration: saa'ada — wal-mu'minu yusaa'idu akhaah

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عَمِلَ — فَالعَمَلُ عِبادَة
lines.english: Amila — for work is worship.
lines.transliteration: amila — fal-amalu ibaada

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: حَسَنٌ. لِنَخْتَبِرْ هَذِهِ الأَفْعال
lines.english: Good. Let us test these verbs.
lines.transliteration: hasanun. linakhtabir haadhihi al-af'aal

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يا بُنَيَّ، هَذا هُوَ دَرْسُكَ الأَخِير
lines.english: My child, this is your final lesson.
lines.transliteration: ya bunayya, haadha huwa darsuka al-akhiir

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لَقَدْ تَعَلَّمْتَ الكَثِير. مِنَ الحُرُوفِ إِلى الكَلِماتِ إِلى الجُمَل
lines.english: You have learned so much. From letters to words to sentences.
lines.transliteration: laqad ta'allamta al-kathiir. min al-huruufi ilaa al-kalimaati ilaa al-jumal

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ — قُلْها دائِماً عِنْدَ النِّعْمَة
lines.english: Alhamdulillah — say it always when blessed.
lines.transliteration: al-hamdu lillaah — qulhaa daa'iman inda an-ni'ma

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَعَ السَّلامَةِ — لِلوَداع
lines.english: Ma'a as-salaama — for farewell.
lines.transliteration: ma'a as-salaama — lil-wadaa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَراكَ لاحِقاً — فَالعِلْمُ لا يَنْتَهِي
lines.english: Araaka laahiqan — for knowledge never ends.
lines.transliteration: araaka laahiqan — fal-ilmu laa yantahii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذا لَيْسَ نِهايَةَ رِحْلَتِكَ. هَذِهِ بِدايَةٌ جَدِيدَة. اِخْتِبارٌ أَخِير!
lines.english: This is not the end of your journey. This is a new beginning. One final test!
lines.transliteration: haadha laysa nihaayata rihlatika. haadhihi bidaayatun jadiida. ikhtibaarun akhiir!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذِهِ المَكْتَبَةُ فِيها آلافُ الكُتُبِ بِالعَرَبِيَّة
lines.english: This library contains thousands of books in Arabic.
lines.transliteration: haadhihi al-maktabatu fiihaa aalaaf al-kutubi bil-arabiyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَنْ يَقْرَأُ يَفْتَحُ أَبْوابَ العالَم
lines.english: Whoever reads opens the doors of the world.
lines.transliteration: man yaqra'u yaftahu abwaab al-aalam

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كُلُّ كِتابٍ هُنا كَنْزٌ. وَأَنتَ الآنَ تَمْلِكُ المِفْتاحَ — اللُّغَةَ العَرَبِيَّة
lines.english: Every book here is a treasure. And you now hold the key — the Arabic language.
lines.transliteration: kullu kitaabin hunaa kanzun. wa anta al-aana tamliku al-miftaaha — al-lughata al-arabiyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الحَمدُ لِلَّه. مَرحَباً يا بُنَيّ
lines.english: Praise be to God. Welcome, my child.
lines.transliteration: al-hamdu lillaah. marhaban ya bunayy

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الوَقتُ نِعمَة مِن الله. لِنَتَعَلَّم
lines.english: Time is a blessing from God. Let us learn.
lines.transliteration: al-waqtu ni'ma min allaah. linata'allam

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يَوْم — كُلّ يَوم فيهِ خَمس صَلَوات
lines.english: Day — every day has five prayers.
lines.transliteration: yawm — kullu yawm fiihi khams salawaat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لَيْل — وَقتُ السُّكون وَالتَّأَمُّل
lines.english: Night — a time of stillness and reflection.
lines.transliteration: layl — waqtu as-sukuun wat-ta'ammul

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: صَباح — وَقتُ صَلاة الفَجر
lines.english: Morning — time for the dawn prayer.
lines.transliteration: sabaah — waqtu salaat al-fajr

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: المَسجِد هُوَ قَلبُ القَريَة
lines.english: The mosque is the heart of the village.
lines.transliteration: al-masjid huwa qalbu al-qarya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هُنا نُصَلّي وَنَتَعَلَّم وَنَجتَمِع
lines.english: Here we pray, learn, and gather.
lines.transliteration: hunaa nusallii wa nata'allam wa najtami'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العِلمُ فَريضَة عَلى كُلّ مُسلِم
lines.english: Knowledge is an obligation for every Muslim.
lines.transliteration: al-'ilmu fariida 'alaa kulli muslim

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: المُزارِع عُمَر يَحتاج مُساعَدَة في الحَصاد
lines.english: Farmer Omar needs help with the harvest.
lines.transliteration: al-muzaari' 'umar yahtaaj musaa'ada fii al-hasaad

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَالشَّيخ يوسُف يُعِدّ دَرساً جَديداً
lines.english: And Sheikh Yusuf is preparing a new lesson.
lines.transliteration: wash-shaykh yuusuf yu'idd darsan jadiidan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: التَّجويدُ حَفِظَ النُّطقَ العَرَبيَّ لِأَكثَرَ مِن أَلفِ عام
lines.english: Tajweed preserved Arabic pronunciation for over a thousand years
lines.transliteration: at-tajwid hafiza an-nutq al-arabi li-akthar min alf 'am
lines.culturalNote: Tajweed (تجويد) is the science of Quranic recitation. Its rules standardized Arabic pronunciation so precisely that Classical Arabic sounds almost identical today to how it sounded in the 7th century.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَفهومُ الفَصاحَة — البَلاغَةُ هِيَ أَعلى فُنونِ اللُّغَة
lines.english: The concept of fasaha — eloquence is the highest art of language
lines.transliteration: mafhum al-fasaha — al-balagha hiya a'la funun al-lugha

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العَرَبيَّةُ لُغَةُ الضّاد — الحَرفُ الَّذي لا يوجَدُ في أَيِّ لُغَةٍ أُخرى
lines.english: Arabic is the language of Daad — a letter found in no other language
lines.transliteration: al-arabiyya lughat ad-daad — al-harf alladhi la yujad fi ayy lugha ukhra
lines.culturalNote: Arabic is called 'lughat ad-Daad' (language of the Daad) because the letter ض is unique to Arabic — no other language has this exact sound.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهلاً، يَا وَلَدي. هَل تَعرِف لِمَاذَا يُسمُّون العَرَبِيَّة "لُغَة الضَّاد"؟
lines.english: Welcome, my child. Do you know why Arabic is called "the language of the Daad"?
lines.transliteration: Ahlan, yaa waladii. Hal ta'rif li-maadha yusammun al-'arabiyya 'lughat ad-daad'?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: حَرف الضَّاد فَريد في اللُّغَة العَرَبِيَّة — لا يوجَد في أَيِّ لُغَة أُخرى بِنَفس الطَّريقَة!
lines.english: The letter Daad is unique to Arabic — it does not exist in any other language in the same way!
lines.transliteration: Harf ad-daad fariid fil-lugha al-'arabiyya — laa yujad fii ayyi lugha ukhraa bi-nafs at-tariqa!
lines.culturalNote: Arabic is called "Lughat ad-Daad" (لُغَة الضَّاد) — the language of the letter Daad — because this emphatic consonant is unique to Arabic. The science of tajweed (تَجويد) preserves the exact Quranic pronunciation as taught by the Prophet, creating an unbroken oral chain of 1,400 years.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عِلم التَّجويد يَحفَظ النُّطق القُرآنِيَّ كَمَا عَلَّمَه النَّبيّ. سِلسِلَة لا تَنقَطِع!
lines.english: The science of tajweed preserves Quranic pronunciation as the Prophet taught it. An unbroken chain!
lines.transliteration: Ilm at-tajwiid yahfaz an-nutq al-qur'aaniyy kamaa 'allamahu an-Nabiyy. Silsila laa tanqati'!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَلَّم: الصَّلاة — كَلِمَة تَربِط العَبد بِرَبِّه. خَمسَ مَرَّات كُلَّ يَوم!
lines.english: Learn: prayer — a word that connects the servant to his Lord. Five times every day!
lines.transliteration: Ta'allam: as-salaah — kalima tarbit al-'abd bi-rabbih. Khamsa marraat kull yawm!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بِسُرور، يَا وَلَدي. الكَلِمَات الدِّينِيَّة هِيَ أَساس اللُّغَة العَرَبِيَّة.
lines.english: With pleasure, my child. Religious words are the foundation of the Arabic language.
lines.transliteration: Bi-suruur, yaa waladii. Al-kalimaat ad-diiniyya hiya asaas al-lugha al-'arabiyya.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: السَّلام عَلَيكُم — أَعظَم تَحِيَّة. نَتَمَنَّى السَّلامَة لِبَعضِنا البَعض في كُلِّ لِقَاء!
lines.english: As-salaamu alaykum — the greatest greeting. We wish safety upon each other in every meeting!
lines.transliteration: As-salaamu 'alaykum — a'zam tahiyya. Natamanna as-salaama li-ba'dinaa al-ba'd fii kulli liqaa'!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الشُّكر — نِصف الإِيمَان. الشَّاكِر يَرى النِّعمَة في كُلِّ شَيء!
lines.english: Thanks — half of faith. The grateful one sees blessing in everything!
lines.transliteration: Ash-shukr — nisf al-iimaan. Ash-shaakir yaraa an-ni'ma fii kulli shay'!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَالصَّبر — أَعظَم فَضِيلَة. قَال الله: "إِنَّ اللهَ مَع الصَّابِرين".
lines.english: And patience — the greatest virtue. God said: "Indeed God is with the patient."
lines.transliteration: Was-sabr — a'zam fadiila. Qaala Allaah: 'Inna Allaaha ma'a as-saabirin'.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحسَنتَ! اللُّغَة والإِيمَان يَسيران مَعاً في الإِسلَام. تَعَلَّم اللُّغَة وَاِفهَم الدِّين أَعمَق.
lines.english: Well done! Language and faith walk together in Islam. Learn the language and understand religion more deeply.
lines.transliteration: Ahsanta! Al-lugha wal-iimaan yasiiraani ma'an fil-islaam. Ta'allam al-lugha wa ifham ad-diin a'maq.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: التَّجويد مِن "جَوَّد" — أَي أَحسَنَ وَأَتقَنَ. هُوَ عِلم إِتقَان النُّطق القُرآنِيّ.
lines.english: Tajweed is from "jawwada" — meaning to perfect and excel. It is the science of mastering Quranic recitation.
lines.transliteration: At-tajwiid min 'jawwada' — ay ahsana wa atqana. Huwa 'ilm itqaan an-nutq al-qur'aaniyy.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كُلُّ حَرف لَه مَخرَج مُعَيَّن — مِن الحَلق أَو اللِّسَان أَو الشَّفَتَين. العِلم الدَّقيق!
lines.english: Every letter has a specific point of articulation — from the throat, tongue, or lips. A precise science!
lines.transliteration: Kullu harf lahu makhraj mu'ayyan — min al-halq aw al-lisaan aw ash-shafatayn. Al-'ilm ad-daqiiq!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: المُقرِئون حَفِظوا النُّطق الأَصلِيَّ لِأَربَعَة عَشَر قَرناً — تَسَلسُل شَفَهِيّ مُذهِل!
lines.english: The Quran reciters preserved the original pronunciation for fourteen centuries — a remarkable oral chain!
lines.transliteration: Al-muqri'uun hafizuu an-nutq al-asliyy li-arba'ata 'ashar qarnan — tasalsul shafawiyy mudhil!
lines.culturalNote: "Allah" is the only word that uses every point of Arabic articulation — from the back of the throat to the lips. Quranic reciters train for years to perfect each sound. The science of tajweed has preserved Classical Arabic pronunciation unchanged since the 7th century CE.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَلَّم: الصَّوت — لِأَنَّ الصَّوت الجَميل يَنفُذ إِلى القَلب قَبلَ المَعنى!
lines.english: Learn: the sound/voice — because a beautiful voice reaches the heart before meaning does!
lines.transliteration: Ta'allam: as-sawt — li-anna as-sawt al-jamiil yanfudh ilaa al-qalb qabla al-ma'naa!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهلاً، يَا وَلَدي. كَيفَ حَالُكَ؟ هَل تَعَلَّمتَ كَلِمَات جَديدَة اليَوم؟
lines.english: Welcome, my child. How are you? Have you learned new words today?
lines.transliteration: Ahlan, yaa waladii. Kayfa haaluk? Hal ta'allamta kalimaat jadiida al-yawm?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَلُّم اللُّغَة العَرَبِيَّة عِبَادَة. كُلُّ كَلِمَة تَعلَّمتَها خَطوَة نَحو فَهم القُرآن.
lines.english: Learning Arabic is an act of worship. Every word you learn is a step toward understanding the Quran.
lines.transliteration: Ta'allum al-lugha al-'arabiyya 'ibaada. Kullu kalima ta'allamtahaa khatwa nahwa fahm al-qur'aan.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَلَّم: اليَوم — لِأَنَّ كُلَّ يَوم هُوَ فُرصَة جَديدَة لِلتَّعلُّم!
lines.english: Learn: today — because every day is a new opportunity to learn!
lines.transliteration: Ta'allam: al-yawm — li-anna kull yawm huwa fursa jadiida lit-ta'allum!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَالغَد — لِأَنَّ ما لَم تَتَعلَّمه اليَوم، فَرصَتُكَ غَداً. لا تُؤَجِّل!
lines.english: And tomorrow — because what you did not learn today, there is your chance tomorrow. Do not delay!
lines.transliteration: Wa al-ghad — li-anna maa lam tata'allamhu al-yawm, fursat اُk ghadan. Laa tu'ajjil!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العَرَبِيَّة لُغَة الضَّاد — حَرف الضَّاد فَريد في العَرَبِيَّة وَحدَها
lines.english: Arabic is the language of the Daad — the Daad letter is unique to Arabic alone.
lines.transliteration: al-arabiyya lughat ad-daad — harf ad-daad fariid fil-arabiyya wahdaha

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لا تَوجَد في أَيّ لُغَة أُخرى — هَذا يَجعَل العَرَبِيَّة فَريدَة
lines.english: It exists in no other language — this makes Arabic unique.
lines.transliteration: laa tujad fii ayy lugha ukhraa — haadha yaj'al al-arabiyya fariida

choices.english: Language of the Daad! Proud to learn it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا ياسمين الخَبّازَة. مَرحَباً!
lines.english: I am Yasmin the baker. Welcome!
lines.transliteration: ana yasmiin al-khabbazza. marhaban!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَخبُزُ مُنذُ طُفولَتي. الخُبزُ يَجمَع النّاس
lines.english: I have been baking since childhood. Bread brings people together.
lines.transliteration: akhbuzu mundhu tufuulatii. al-khubzu yajma' an-naas

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بِسْمِ الله! ماذا نَطبُخ اليَوم؟
lines.english: In God's name! What shall we cook today?
lines.transliteration: bismillaah! maadha natbukh al-yawm?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: المَطبَخ مَدرَسَة! لِنَتَعَلَّم
lines.english: The kitchen is a school! Let us learn.
lines.transliteration: al-matbakh madrasa! linata'allam

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَرُزّ — نَأكُلُهُ مَع كُلّ شَيء
lines.english: Rice — we eat it with everything.
lines.transliteration: aruzz — na'kuluhu ma' kulli shay'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: دَجاج — الطَّبَق المُفَضَّل في الواحَة
lines.english: Chicken — the favorite dish in the oasis.
lines.transliteration: dajaaj — at-tabaq al-mufaddal fii al-waaha

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أُمّي عَلَّمَتني الخَبز وَأَنا صَغيرَة
lines.english: My mother taught me baking when I was little.
lines.transliteration: ummii 'allamatnii al-khabz wa ana saghiira

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: في رَمَضان نَخبُز طُوال اللَّيل لِلجيران
lines.english: In Ramadan we bake all night for the neighbors.
lines.transliteration: fii ramadaan nakhbuz tuwaal al-layl lil-jiiraan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الإِمام مُحَمَّد يُحِبّ خُبزي بِالزَّعتَر
lines.english: Imam Muhammad loves my za'atar bread.
lines.transliteration: al-imaam muhammad yuhibb khubzii biz-za'tar

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَالعَشّابَة خَديجَة تَطلُب خُبزاً بِدون مِلح
lines.english: And Herbalist Khadija orders bread without salt.
lines.transliteration: wal-'ashhaaba khadiija tatlub khubzan biduun milh

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَرحَباً ثانِيَة! اليَوم نَتَعَلَّم الحَلَويّات
lines.english: Welcome back! Today we learn sweets.
lines.transliteration: marhaban thaaniya! al-yawm nata'allam al-halawiyyaat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سُكَّر — وَكَلِمَة "sugar" الإنجليزِيَّة جاءَت مِن "sukkar" العَرَبِيَّة
lines.english: Sukkar — sugar. The English word "sugar" came from Arabic "sukkar".
lines.transliteration: sukkar — wa kalima "sugar" al-injliiziyya jaa'at min "sukkar" al-arabiyya
lines.culturalNote: "Sugar" traces through Arabic sukkar (سُكَّر) from Sanskrit sharkara. Arab merchants introduced sugar refining to Europe in the medieval period. The word "candy" also comes from Arabic qand (قَنْد, crystallized sugar).

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: حَلوى — كُلّ شَيء حُلو! مِن "حَلال" وَ"حَلاوَة"
lines.english: Halwa — sweets! Related to halaal and halaawa (sweetness).
lines.transliteration: halwaa — kull shay' hulw! min "halaal" wa "halaawa"

choices.english: My tongue wants sweets now! Thank you.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهلاً مَرَّة ثانِيَة! الفُرن ساخِن وَعِندي دَرس جَديد
lines.english: Welcome again! The oven is hot and I have a new lesson.
lines.transliteration: ahlan marra thaaniya! al-furn saakhin wa 'indii dars jadiid

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قَهوَة — المَشروب المُقَدَّس في العالَم العَرَبي
lines.english: Qahwa — coffee, the sacred drink in the Arab world.
lines.transliteration: qahwa — al-mashrob al-muqaddas fil-'aalam al-'arabii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَكَلِمَة "coffee" الإنجليزِيَّة جاءَت مِن "قَهوَة" العَرَبِيَّة
lines.english: The English word "coffee" came from Arabic "qahwa".
lines.transliteration: wa kalima "coffee" al-injliiziyya jaa'at min "qahwa" al-arabiyya
lines.culturalNote: "Coffee" derives from Arabic qahwa (قَهوَة). Coffee originated in Ethiopia but Arab merchants popularized it worldwide from 15th century Yemen. The first coffeehouses (qahwakhaana) opened in Mecca around 1450 CE, creating the world's first "café culture".

choices.english: Now I want coffee! Thank you, Yasmin.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل تَعرِف "رَمَضان"؟ شَهر الصِّيام وَالعَطاء
lines.english: Do you know "Ramadan"? The month of fasting and giving.
lines.transliteration: hal ta'rif "ramadaan"? shahr as-siyaam wal-'ataa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: فِي رَمَضان نَأكُل "سُحور" قَبلَ الفَجر وَ"إِفطار" عِندَ الغُروب
lines.english: In Ramadan we eat "suhoor" before dawn and "iftar" at sunset.
lines.transliteration: fii ramadaan na'kul "suhoor" qabl al-fajr wa "iftaar" 'inda al-ghuroob

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَكَلِمَة "مُهمَّش" تَعني الحَرَكات فَوق الحُروف — مِنها جاءَت harakat
lines.english: Vowel marks in Arabic are called harakat — "movements" over letters.
lines.transliteration: harakat al-huroof — harakaat — "movements" fawq al-huroof

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الخُبز في العَرَبِيَّة — "عَيْش" في مِصر — أَي "حَياة"
lines.english: Bread in Egypt is called "aysh" — meaning "life".
lines.transliteration: al-khubz fil-arabiyya — "'aysh" fii misr — ay "hayaat"

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَفي الخَليج "خُبز" — نَفس الجَذر لِلعَيش وَالحَياة
lines.english: And in the Gulf "khubz" — the same root as 'aysh meaning life.
lines.transliteration: wa fil-khalij "khubz" — nafs al-jadhr lil-'aysh wal-hayaat

choices.english: Bread is life! Thank you, Yasmin.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا يارا. أَعتَني بِالخُيول مُنذُ صِغَري
lines.english: I am Yara. I have cared for horses since I was small.
lines.transliteration: ana yaaraa. a'tanii bil-khuyuul mundhu sigharii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَيّا! الخُيول تَنتَظِر. ماذا تُريد؟
lines.english: Let's go! The horses are waiting. What do you want?
lines.transliteration: hayyaa! al-khuyuul tantazir. maadha turiid?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الحَيَوانات أَصدِقاؤنا! لِنَتَعَلَّم أَسماءَها
lines.english: Animals are our friends! Let us learn their names.
lines.transliteration: al-hayawaanaat asdiqaa'unaa! linata'allam asmaa'ahaa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: حِصان — أَنبَل الحَيَوانات
lines.english: Horse — the noblest of animals.
lines.transliteration: hisaan — anbal al-hayawaanaat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: جَمَل — سَفينَة الصَّحراء
lines.english: Camel — the ship of the desert.
lines.transliteration: jamal — safiinat as-sahraa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: طَيْر — حُرّ في السَّماء
lines.english: Bird — free in the sky.
lines.transliteration: tayr — hurr fis-samaa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الحِصانُ العَرَبي أَجمَل سُلالَة في العالَم
lines.english: The Arabian horse is the most beautiful breed in the world.
lines.transliteration: al-hisaanu al-'arabii ajmal sulaala fii al-'aalam

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يَقولون أَنَّ الله خَلَقَهُ مِن الرّيح
lines.english: They say God created it from the wind.
lines.transliteration: yaquuluun anna allaah khalaqahu min ar-riih

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قافِلَة جَديدَة وَصَلَت مِن الجَبَل
lines.english: A new caravan arrived from the mountain.
lines.transliteration: qaafila jadiida wasalat min al-jabal

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يَقولون إِنَّ الطَّريق خَطير هَذِهِ الأَيّام
lines.english: They say the road is dangerous these days.
lines.transliteration: yaquuluun inna at-tariiq khatiir haadhihi al-ayyaam

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَرحَباً! الخُيول تَفرَح بِرُجوعِك
lines.english: Welcome! The horses are happy at your return.
lines.transliteration: marhaban! al-khuyuul tafrahu bi-rujooo'ik

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قافِلَة — مَجموعَة مِن الجِمال وَالتُّجّار
lines.english: Qaafila — a caravan, a group of camels and traders.
lines.transliteration: qaafila — majmoo'a min al-jimaal wat-tujjaar

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَكَلِمَة "caravan" الإنجليزِيَّة جاءَت مِن الفارِسِيَّة عَن طَريق العَرَبِيَّة: "قَرواَن"
lines.english: "Caravan" in English came through Arabic from Persian: "qirwaan".
lines.transliteration: "caravan" al-injliiziyya jaa'at min al-faarisiyya 'an tariiq al-arabiyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: طَريق الحَرير كانَ أَطوَل طَريق تِجاري في التّاريخ — مِن الصّين إلى الأَندَلُس
lines.english: The Silk Road was the longest trade route in history — from China to Andalusia.
lines.transliteration: tariiq al-hariir kaana atwal tariiq tijaarii fit-taariikh — min as-siin ilaa al-andalus
lines.culturalNote: The Silk Road (طَريق الحَرير) connected China to Andalusia. Arab merchants were its backbone from the 8th-13th centuries, carrying silk, spices, paper, and knowledge — along with Arabic vocabulary that remains in dozens of languages today.

choices.english: I want to travel someday! Thank you, Yara.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَرحَباً مَرَّة ثانِيَة! الإِسطَبل مَكان يُعَلِّم
lines.english: Welcome again! The stable is a place that teaches.
lines.transliteration: marhaban marra thaaniya! al-istab al-makaan yu'allim

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الحِصان العَرَبي الأَصيل — أَسرَع خَيل في العالَم القَديم
lines.english: The Arabian thoroughbred — the fastest horse in the ancient world.
lines.transliteration: al-hisaan al-arabii al-asiil — asra' khayl fil-'aalam al-qadiim

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اللُّغَة العَرَبِيَّة عِندَها مِئَة اِسم لِلحِصان وَخَمسِمِئَة لِلأَسَد
lines.english: Arabic has one hundred names for the horse and five hundred for the lion.
lines.transliteration: al-lugha al-arabiyya 'indahaa mi'a ism lil-hisaan wa khamsumi'a lil-asad
lines.culturalNote: Classical Arabic's richness of vocabulary is legendary: reportedly 1,000+ words for camel and its states, 500+ for lion, 200+ for snake. This reflects the Bedouin oral tradition of precision in describing the natural world upon which survival depended.

choices.arabic: اللُّغَة العَرَبِيَّة غَنِيَّة جِدَّاً! شُكراً يارا
choices.english: Arabic is so rich! Thank you, Yara.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الجَمَل — سَفينَة الصَّحراء — يُخزِّن الدَّهن في سَنامِه لَيسَ الماء
lines.english: The camel — ship of the desert — stores fat in its hump, not water.
lines.transliteration: al-jamal — safinat as-sahraa' — yukhazzin ad-dahn fii sanamih laysa al-maa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العَرَب سَمَّوا الجَمَل "سَفينَة الصَّحراء" — وَهُوَ وَسيلَة نَقلِهِم لِأَلفَي سَنَة
lines.english: Arabs called the camel "ship of the desert" — their transport for two thousand years.
lines.transliteration: al-arab sammaaw al-jamal "safinat as-sahraa'" — wa huwa wasiilat naqlihim li-alfay sana
lines.culturalNote: The camel's domestication around 3000 BCE transformed the Arabian peninsula. Classical Arabic has reportedly over 1,000 words related to camels and their states — reflecting the animal's centrality to Bedouin survival.

choices.english: The camel is a miracle! Thank you, Yara.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: "الجَزيرَة العَرَبِيَّة" تَعني: الجَزيرَة — الأَرض المُحاطَة بِالماء
lines.english: "Al-Jazira al-Arabiyya" means: jazira — land surrounded by water (peninsula).
lines.transliteration: "al-jazira al-arabiyya" ta'nii: al-jaziira — al-ard al-muhaata bil-maa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: "الجَزيرَة" أَيضاً اِسم قَناة الأَخبار — مَعناها "الجَزيرَة"
lines.english: "Al-Jazeera" is also the news channel name — it means "The Island/Peninsula".
lines.transliteration: "al-jazeera" aydan ism qanaat al-akhbaar — ma'naaha "al-jaziira"

choices.english: Al-Jazeera! I understand now. Thank you, Yara.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلاً وَسَهْلاً! لَقَد دَخَلتَ مَكاناً خاصّاً
lines.english: Welcome! You have entered a special place.
lines.transliteration: ahlan wa sahlan! laqad dakhalta makaanan khaassan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هُنا أَحتَفِظُ بِأَثمَنِ الكُتُبِ وَالمَخطوطات
lines.english: Here I keep my most precious books and manuscripts.
lines.transliteration: hunaa ahtafizu bi-athmani al-kutubi wal-makhtootaat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لِنَتَعَلَّم التَّحِيّاتِ الرَّسمِيَّة
lines.english: Let us learn formal greetings.
lines.transliteration: linata'allam at-tahiyyaati ar-rasmiyya

choices.english: I want to look around first

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عُدتَ مَرَّة أُخرى! هَل تُريدُ أَن نُكمِل؟
lines.english: You're back again! Shall we continue?
lines.transliteration: udta marratan ukhraa! hal turiidu an nukmil?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العِلمُ لا يَنتَهي أَبَداً
lines.english: Knowledge never ends.
lines.transliteration: al-ilmu laa yantahii abadan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَوَّلاً: تَشَرَّفنا — عِندَ المُقابَلَة الأولى
lines.english: First: tasharrafnaa — when meeting for the first time.
lines.transliteration: awwalan: tasharrafnaa — inda al-muqaabala al-uulaa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ثانِياً: حَيّاكَ الله — تَحِيَّة كَريمَة
lines.english: Second: hayyaaka allaah — a noble greeting.
lines.transliteration: thaaniyan: hayyaaka allaah — tahiyyatun kariima

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مُمتاز! تَعَلَّمتَ تَحِيّاتٍ رَسمِيَّة
lines.english: Excellent! You have learned formal greetings.
lines.transliteration: mumtaaz! ta'allamta tahiyyaatin rasmiyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَرْحَباً في بَيتي! هُنا أَعيشُ مَعَ عائِلَتي
lines.english: Welcome to my home! I live here with my family.
lines.transliteration: marhaban fii baytii! hunaa a'iishu ma'a 'aa'ilatii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل تَعرِف كَلِمات العائِلَة بِالعَرَبِيَّة؟
lines.english: Do you know family words in Arabic?
lines.transliteration: hal ta'rif kalimaat al-'aa'ila bil-'arabiyya?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعالَ أُعَلِّمك!
lines.english: Come, let me teach you!
lines.transliteration: ta'aala u'allimak!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلاً مَرَّة ثانِيَة! العائِلَة هِيَ كُلّ شَيء
lines.english: Welcome again! Family is everything.
lines.transliteration: ahlan marratan thaaniya! al-'aa'ila hiya kullu shay'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل نَتَعَلَّم كَلِمات جَديدَة؟
lines.english: Shall we learn new words?
lines.transliteration: hal nata'allam kalimaat jadiida?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أُمّ — هَذِهِ أَغلى كَلِمَة
lines.english: Umm — this is the most precious word (mother).
lines.transliteration: umm — haadhihi aghlaa kalima

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَب — الرَّجُل الكَبير في البَيت
lines.english: Ab — the elder man of the house (father).
lines.transliteration: ab — ar-rajul al-kabiir fil-bayt

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَخ — مِثل صَديق لَكِن مِنَ الدَّم
lines.english: Akh — like a friend but from blood (brother).
lines.transliteration: akh — mithl sadiiq laakin mina ad-dam

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أُخت — البِنت مِن نَفس العائِلَة
lines.english: Ukht — the girl from the same family (sister).
lines.transliteration: ukht — al-bint min nafs al-'aa'ila

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الرِّحلَة إلى المَعرِفَة تَبدَأ بِخُطوَة
lines.english: The journey to knowledge begins with a step.
lines.transliteration: ar-rihla ilaa al-ma'rifa tabda' bi-khutwa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا مُسافِر. رَأَيتُ بِلاداً كَثيرَة وَتَعَلَّمتُ لُغاتٍ كَثيرَة
lines.english: I am a traveler. I have seen many lands and learned many languages.
lines.transliteration: ana musaafir. ra'aytu bilaadan kathiira wa ta'allamtu lughaat kathiira

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العَرَبِيَّة — لُغَة الشِّعر وَالحِكمَة وَالعِلم
lines.english: Arabic — the language of poetry, wisdom, and science.
lines.transliteration: al-arabiyya — lughat ash-shi'r wal-hikma wal-'ilm

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: رَحَلتُ مِن الأَندَلُس إلى بَغداد — شَهرَيْن عَلى الجَمَل
lines.english: I traveled from Andalusia to Baghdad — two months on camel.
lines.transliteration: rahaltu min al-andalus ilaa baghdaad — shahrayn 'alaa al-jamal
lines.culturalNote: The medieval Islamic world was connected by vast trade and pilgrimage routes. Traveling from Cordoba in Andalusia (Spain) to Baghdad took months by camel caravan.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: في كُلّ مَدينَة تَعَلَّمتُ كَلِمات جَديدَة — التُّجّار يَتَحَدَّثون العَرَبِيَّة في كُلّ مَكان
lines.english: In every city I learned new words — traders speak Arabic everywhere.
lines.transliteration: fii kull madiina ta'allamtu kalimaat jadiida — at-tujjaar yatahadathoon al-arabiyya fii kull makaan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سَفَر — هَذِهِ كَلِمَة مُهِمَّة لِلمُسافِر
lines.english: Safar — this is an important word for a traveler.
lines.transliteration: safar — haadhihi kalima muhimma lil-musaafir

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَكَلِمَة "safari" الإنجليزِيَّة جاءَت مِن العَرَبِيَّة — سَفَري
lines.english: And the English word "safari" came from Arabic — safarii (my journey).
lines.transliteration: wa kalima "safari" al-injliiziyya jaa'at min al-arabiyya — safarii
lines.culturalNote: "Safari" comes from Arabic safar (سَفَر, journey). Arab merchants and explorers established the trade routes across East Africa that later European explorers would follow.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كُلّ يَوم جَديد فُرصَة لِلتَّعَلُّم
lines.english: Every new day is an opportunity to learn.
lines.transliteration: kull yawm jadiid fursa lit-ta'allum

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: المَنطِقَة آمِنَة. تَوَقَّف عِندَ الحاجَة
lines.english: The area is safe. Stop if you need anything.
lines.transliteration: al-mantiqа aamina. tawqqaf 'inda al-haaja

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا الحارِس اللَّيلي. أَحمي المَدينَة مِن الغُروب إلى الفَجر
lines.english: I am the night guard. I protect the city from sunset to dawn.
lines.transliteration: ana al-haaris al-laylii. ahmi al-madiina min al-ghuroob ilaa al-fajr

choices.arabic: هَل تَعلَم شَيئاً عَن هَذِهِ المَدينَة؟
choices.english: Do you know something about this city?
How do you say "safety" in Arabic?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذِهِ المَدينَة قَديمَة جِدَّاً. بُنِيَت قَبلَ مِئَة وَخَمسين سَنَة
lines.english: This city is very old. It was built 150 years ago.
lines.transliteration: haadhihi al-madiina qadiima jiddan. buniyat qabla mi'a wa khamsiin sana

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الحُراسُ الأَوائِل كانوا يَحفَظون القُرآن — كانَت تِلاوَتُهُم تُبعِد الشَّرّ
lines.english: The first guards memorized the Quran — their recitation was said to ward off evil.
lines.transliteration: al-hurrasu al-awaa'il kaanuu yahfazoon al-qur'an — kaanat tilaawatuhum tub'id ash-sharr

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَمَان — هَذِهِ الكَلِمَة الجَميلَة
lines.english: Amaan — this beautiful word.
lines.transliteration: amaan — haadhihi al-kalima al-jamiila

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَكَلِمَة "آمِن" تَعني safe — نَفس الجَذر: أ-م-ن
lines.english: And "aamin" means safe — same root: A-M-N.
lines.transliteration: wa kalima "aamin" ta'nii safe — nafs al-jadhr: a-m-n

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الجَذر العَرَبي يُعطيك عَشَرات الكَلِمات مِن ثَلاثَة حُروف
lines.english: The Arabic root gives you dozens of words from three letters.
lines.transliteration: al-jadhr al-arabii yu'tiika 'asharaat al-kalimaat min thalaatha huroof
lines.culturalNote: The Arabic root system (trilateral roots) is one of the most systematic in the world. The root A-M-N (أ-م-ن) generates: amaan (safety), aamin (safe), mu'min (believer), iimaan (faith), amiin (trustworthy).

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهلاً بِكَ يا مُسافِر — الشِّعرُ طَريقُ القَلب
lines.english: Welcome, traveller — poetry is the path of the heart

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل تُريدُ أَن تَخوضَ مُسابَقَةَ الشِّعر مَعي؟
lines.english: Would you like to enter a poetry contest with me?
